hero: copy affordance on the full hash — no visible control beside 0x27a6c250…29a6c

findings.location: hero, between the full hash line and the Generate trace card; and the Overview grid
findings.finding: Three Must-show items are absent. There is no age or timestamp anywhere on the page — the hero runs eyebrow, truncated hash, status badge, full hash, then straight into the trace card, and the Overview grid's seven rows are Data, Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost·Mana. There is no visible copy affordance on the full hash. Transaction type is never labelled; it exists only as "kind": "public-avm-call" inside the raw JSON, which is not a labelled overview fact.

findings.location: hero — the h1 "0x27a6…9a6c" and the full hash line directly beneath it
findings.finding: The largest type on the page carries the least information. The h1 is a 4+4-character abbreviation set at roughly 28px monospace, and the full 42-character value it abbreviates sits 20px below it at body size in the same face. Two consecutive lines of the same string at two sizes read as a duplication rather than a hierarchy, and the display slot is spent on a value the reader can already see in full.

findings.location: section headings — Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes, Raw (chain-native)
findings.finding: All six headings are set at one size and one weight, so the eight-section scroll has a flat spine with no second level. Nothing in the type says that Events, Internal calls and State changes are three peers of the same kind while Overview and Raw are the page's bookends; that distinction is currently carried only by whether a horizontal rule happens to sit above the heading. The expectation block asks the eye to find hero → action → overview without reading, and past the fold there is no typographic ranking to navigate by.

findings.location: badges — "Synthetic demo data" in the Data row vs "Succeeded" (hero), "On demand" (trace card), "Yes" (Canonical), "Pending" (Finality)
findings.finding: One component, two type treatments. The provenance badge is monospace and letterspaced; the four status badges are proportional sans at a smaller size with no tracking. Because the provenance badge is the one graded as content, its differing face reads as a different kind of object rather than as the same badge primitive carrying the most important claim on the page.

findings.location: footer, the data-disclosure paragraph beginning "No account, no tracking."
findings.finding: This line runs the full content width — roughly 120 characters before it wraps — while every other paragraph on the page (the trace note, the provenance sentences, the ABI note, the three section explanations) is held to a 60–75 character measure inside a card. The one paragraph set to the full column is the one the reader is least primed to read.

findings.location: Overview and Decoded input grids, label column (DATA, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST · MANA, SELECTOR, RAW)
findings.finding: The labels are set at roughly 10px uppercase with wide tracking in a light grey. At a 1920px viewport with this much surrounding whitespace the label column is the only wayfinding into a seven-row grid, and it is the smallest and lightest text on the page — one step up in size or one step down in tracking would let the column be scanned rather than read.

missing: hero: age / transaction timestamp — not present in the hero or anywhere else on the page
hero: copy affordance on the full hash — no visible control beside the 42-character value
overview grid: transaction type — not a labelled row; it appears only as "kind" inside the raw JSON

findings.location: hero block between the full hash and the trace card; Overview grid rows
findings.finding: Three Must-show items are absent. The hero runs breadcrumb, eyebrow, truncated hash + status, full hash, and then the trace card, with no age or timestamp at any point; no timestamp appears elsewhere on the page either. The full hash line carries no visible copy control. The Overview grid's rows are Data, Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost·Mana — transaction type is not among them and survives only as a JSON key in the raw section.

findings.location: vertical rhythm across all six section headings and the four section rules
findings.finding: The section spacing is not one scale. The gap from a heading down to its first content block is ~22px above the Overview and Decoded input grids, ~40px above the Events / Internal calls / State changes cards, and ~48px above the raw JSON block — three values for one relationship. The gap from the block above up to a section rule is ~108px before the Overview, Decoded input and Events rules, then ~81px before the Raw (chain-native) rule. A reader scrolling eight sections is given four different measurements for the same two joints.

findings.location: the Events / Internal calls / State changes group, at the Internal calls and State changes headings
findings.finding: Each of these headings sits ~62px below the card belonging to the previous section and ~40px above its own card — a ratio of about 1.6. That is not enough separation for proximity to do the grouping: the heading reads as almost equidistant between the block it does not belong to and the block it does. This is the rubric's named failure case, and it is the one place on the page where three sections share a single rule-delimited band and therefore depend entirely on spacing to be told apart.

findings.location: content column right edge — trace card, ABI note, Events / Internal calls / State changes cards vs the Overview grid, Decoded input grid, raw JSON block and the four section rules
findings.finding: Two right edges alternate down the page. The rules, both grids and the raw block terminate at the content edge (~911px column); the trace card and the four notice cards stop ~295px short of it. The alternation happens five times, and it is not readable as a rule: the widest prose measure on the page is the provenance paragraph, which sits inside the full-width grid, while the narrower notes sit in the narrow cards. The result is a ragged right that looks like two layouts interleaved rather than a decision about measure.

findings.location: Overview grid, the Data row against the six rows beneath it
findings.finding: The Data row is ~144px tall — a badge plus a four-line paragraph — sitting directly above six fact rows of ~37px each. The grid's row rhythm is therefore broken by its own first row, and the visual weight of the section is roughly half provenance prose and half facts. Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target and Cost·Mana read as a short tail hanging off the paragraph rather than as the section's content. If the row is meant to carry the provenance claim that a band used to carry, it is doing so by importing a band's proportions into a facts grid.

findings.location: page shell at the 1920px viewport
findings.finding: The page renders as a single ~911px column centred with roughly 500px of empty canvas on each side, over a 2733px scroll. Nothing in the layout distinguishes this viewport from a 1024px one — the two short grids (seven rows and two rows) and the five-line raw block all sit in one stack. The wide viewport is not being used badly, but it is not being used.

findings.location: footer, right-hand column and the footer's outer padding
findings.finding: The two lines of the right column start at different text left edges: the 'Built with … Powered by CodeTracer' line begins at the column edge, while 'Source on GitHub' is pushed ~14px right because the GitHub mark leads it, so the two lines do not share a left edge. Separately the footer's top padding (~53px from the top border to the first line) is noticeably larger than its bottom padding (~33px below the disclosure), so the block that closes the page sits high in its own band.

hero: copy affordance on the full hash — no visible control
overview grid: transaction type — not a labelled row; present only as a JSON key in the raw section

findings.location: hero, between the full hash and the trace card; Overview grid row list
findings.finding: Three Must-show items are absent. No age or timestamp appears in the hero or anywhere else on the page. The full hash line carries no visible copy control. The Overview grid's rows are Data, Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost·Mana; transaction type is not labelled anywhere and survives only as "kind": "public-avm-call" inside the raw JSON.

findings.location: the indigo accent, across the Generate trace button, the On demand badge, the Synthetic demo data badge in the Data row, the 102:0 block link, the breadcrumb links and all six footer links
findings.finding: One hue carries four unrelated roles: primary action, interactive link, trace-state indicator, and the provenance claim. The Synthetic demo data badge is indigo text inside a thin indigo outline — chromatically the same object as the On demand badge 300px above it and the same colour as every link on the page, so the only element on this page graded as content rather than decoration is rendered in the page's clickable colour and reads as a chip you could press. It also is not in the neutral tone: the demonstrable neutral on this page is the grey pill used by Yes and Pending. A claim that these hashes exist on no network should be the one badge whose colour is used for nothing else.

findings.location: Overview and Decoded input grids, label column (DATA, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST · MANA, SELECTOR, RAW)
findings.finding: This is the page's weakest text-on-surface pair: a mid grey label set on the label column's grey fill, at roughly 3:1–3.5:1 by eye and well under the small-text floor. Every other text pair on the page is near-black on white and comfortable, so the contrast budget has been spent everywhere except on the one column that names what each value is. The grey fill sits only a step or two off the page canvas as well, so the column is doing less separating than it costs in legibility.

findings.location: site nav, the resolver field with placeholder "block · tx · address"
findings.finding: The only input on the page is the least visible element in the header. Its fill is a light grey barely separated from the white nav surface, so the control is carried almost entirely by a 1px border, and the placeholder is a grey on that grey — the lowest-contrast text in the chrome and lower than the nav's own Chains/About labels. Placeholder state is where a light theme most often reveals that its greys were picked against white rather than against the surface they land on, and that is what has happened here.

findings.location: surface levels — the trace card, ABI note and the three section notice cards vs the Overview grid, Decoded input grid and the raw JSON block
findings.finding: Elevation does not encode anything. White boxes sitting on the same canvas appear both with a soft drop shadow (all five cards) and with a border alone (both grids, the raw block), and the two treatments meet inside a single section: the Decoded input grid is flat and the ABI note directly beneath it is elevated, though both are informational surfaces at the same level of the hierarchy. With a fourth grey in play for the raw block's fill, the page has four surface signals — canvas, white, grey fill, shadow — and no readable rule mapping them to roles.

findings.location: Overview grid, the Canonical "Yes" badge and the Finality "Pending" badge
findings.finding: A settled boolean and an unsettled phase share one grey pill. Canonical: Yes is a resolved fact; Finality: Pending is explicitly not resolved yet, and on this page it is the value most likely to change. Rendering them identically means the neutral tone covers both 'this is true' and 'this is not decided', and the only status hue actually in use (the green of Succeeded) sits far above in the hero where it cannot be compared against them.

findings.location: site nav (Chains, About) vs breadcrumb (Home, aztec), Overview (102:0) and footer links
findings.finding: Two link treatments coexist. The nav items are near-black with no underline and no accent; every other link on the page is indigo and underlined. The distinction between navigation and inline link is defensible, but as rendered a reader learns 'indigo + underline means link' from the breadcrumb three lines below a header where the links are neither.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block
findings.finding: The page's only preformatted region is entirely flat: keys, string values and punctuation are all one near-black, and the block's grey fill is close enough to the page canvas that its containment rests on a 1px border. Even without full editor tokens, one step of separation between key and value — and one more step between the block's surface and the canvas — would let the reader parse it at a glance and would make the region look contained rather than merely outlined.

missing: Hero: age — no timestamp or relative age appears anywhere on the page
Overview grid: transaction type — no labelled row, though the raw JSON carries "kind": "public-avm-call"
Decoded input: the 'supply an ABI' action — the note describes supplying an ABI but provides no control

findings.location: hero, between the `Succeeded` badge and the full hash line, and the Overview grid
findings.finding: The transaction's age is absent from the whole page. The hero shows only eyebrow, truncated hash, status badge and full hash; the Overview grid's seven rows are DATA, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST·MANA. There is no timestamp and no relative age in either place, so nothing on this page says when the transaction happened — the one fact a reader uses to decide whether `Pending` finality is a second old or a week old.

findings.location: Overview grid, missing row (would sit near BLOCK / COST·MANA)
findings.finding: Transaction type is not a labelled row in the Overview grid. The value exists on the page — the Raw (chain-native) block at the foot prints "kind": "public-avm-call" — so the page holds the fact but only in the preformatted region a reader is least likely to parse. The labelled-facts surface is the place the expectation puts it.

findings.location: Decoded input section, the bordered note below the SELECTOR / RAW rows
findings.finding: The note's second sentence, 'Supplying an ABI decodes them', names a remedy with no control anywhere in the section to carry it out — no button, link or upload target. The expectation requires a 'supply an ABI' action, and the panel supplies a description of one instead.

findings.location: Events, Internal calls and State changes sections, the vertical run below the Decoded input note
findings.finding: Three consecutive sections each spend an H2 plus a full-width bordered card on a single two-line sentence, and the run costs roughly 500 px of scroll — about half a viewport at 1080 — to deliver 46 words. One of those sentences, 'Internal calls come from the execution trace', restates a line already printed inside the trace card near the top of the page, so the reader scrolls half a screen to be told something the page told them at the fold. The statements are required and correct; the space they are given is not proportional to what they carry, and the identical card shape three times makes the run read as one repeated block rather than three sections.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row (first row)
findings.finding: The DATA row is a badge plus four lines of prose set at the same size as the value column, making it roughly 3.5x the height of every other row in the grid. The eye entering 'Overview' meets a paragraph, and the six scannable facts begin about 130 px into the grid. The provenance sentences are content and belong on the page; setting them at value-column size inside the facts grid is what breaks the grid's row rhythm at its head, and a smaller secondary size under the badge would keep both the claim and the scan.

findings.location: hero, H1 and the monospace line directly beneath it
findings.finding: The same identifier is printed twice about 30 px apart: `0x27a6…9a6c` as the H1 and the full 42-character hash immediately below it. At this viewport the content column is roughly 910 px wide and the full hash would fit as the heading, so the truncated form buys nothing here and costs a line of vertical in the densest part of the page. Truncation earns its place in a table row; in a hero that also prints the full value it is a duplicate.

missing: Hero: age — no timestamp or relative age anywhere on the page
Overview grid: transaction type — no labelled row, though the raw JSON carries "kind": "public-avm-call"
Decoded input: the 'supply an ABI' action — the note describes supplying an ABI but offers no control that does it

findings.location: Decoded input section, the bordered note below the SELECTOR / RAW rows
findings.finding: The note reads 'This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds, so the parameters are shown as raw bytes. Supplying an ABI decodes them.' There is no button, link or upload control in the card or anywhere in the section — the second sentence names a remedy the page provides no path to. The expectation requires an action, not a description of one, and in this product's copy register a stated fix the reader cannot take is the same failure shape as a retry that cannot succeed: the sentence is true and the page is still not honest about what the reader can do next.

findings.location: hero, between the `Succeeded` badge and the full hash line, and the Overview grid
findings.finding: The transaction's age is absent from the entire page. The hero carries eyebrow, truncated hash, status badge and full hash; the grid runs DATA, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST·MANA. With `Pending` finality shown and no time anywhere, the page states a provisional condition without letting a reader judge how provisional it is.

findings.location: Overview grid, missing row
findings.finding: Transaction type has no labelled row in the Overview grid. The fact is on the page only inside the Raw (chain-native) block as "kind": "public-avm-call", so the labelled-facts surface — the part of the page written for a reader rather than for a machine — omits what kind of transaction this is.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row — the `Synthetic demo data` badge — against the `On demand` chip in the trace card, the `102:0` block link and the breadcrumb links
findings.finding: The provenance badge is drawn in the same indigo-blue outline-on-white vocabulary as the `On demand` trace-state chip, and in the same hue as every link on the page and the Generate trace button. The brand accent is therefore doing four jobs at once — primary action, routine state, hyperlink, and the single claim about whether these hashes exist on any network. The row's sentences carry the claim well, but a reader scanning the grid meets a chip that looks exactly like the state chip two sections above it and slides past. Answering the question the row was moved here to answer: the row is enough to be found by someone reading the grid, and not enough to stop someone skimming it, because nothing about its treatment is reserved to provenance.

findings.location: hero `Succeeded` badge, trace card `On demand` chip, grid `Synthetic demo data` / `Yes` / `Pending` badges
findings.finding: One badge primitive is rendered two ways within 400 px of vertical: `On demand` is a full-radius pill with a leading status dot, while `Succeeded`, `Synthetic demo data`, `Yes` and `Pending` are rounded rectangles without one. Three outline colours (green, indigo, grey) is a defensible role split; two geometries for the same primitive is not, and the pill-with-dot reads as a different component family rather than a different state of the same one.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section, the preformatted JSON block
findings.finding: The only preformatted region on the page is set entirely in flat near-black monospace — keys, string values and punctuation identical. This is the page's one opportunity to take the product lineage's editor tokens into an explorer-register surface, the brief's single sanctioned register crossing, and it is spent on monochrome. Chain-native JSON is data rather than source, so this is a preference rather than a violation, but tokenising the keys would say 'CodeTracer' at no cost to the explorer register.

missing: Hero: age — no timestamp or relative age anywhere on the page
Overview grid: transaction type — no labelled row, though the raw JSON carries "kind": "public-avm-call"
Decoded input: the 'supply an ABI' action — the note describes supplying an ABI but provides no control

findings.location: the hero — from the `TRANSACTION` eyebrow through the `0x27a6…9a6c` H1, the `Succeeded` badge and the full-hash line, above the trace card
findings.finding: The hero is the weakest element on the page: it holds the top of the layout and delivers one fact and one identifier printed twice. The required age is absent from it and from the whole page, so nothing tells a reader when this transaction happened; the finality badge has been moved out into the Overview grid, so the hero asserts `Succeeded` while `Pending` waits seven rows below the fold-adjacent grid head; and the full hash below the H1 carries no visible copy affordance while duplicating the truncated value directly above it. The most prominent element on the page is therefore its emptiest, and its omissions are not cosmetic — a reader who reads only the hero leaves believing a pending transaction is settled and cannot date it at all.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — the paragraph beginning "Every block, transaction, address and hash…" (x≈1160–1432, y≈240–555)
findings.finding: The provenance sentences are set flush-right, ragged-left, across eleven lines in a ~28-character measure, because the row inherits the value column's right alignment. Every line begins at a different x, so the reader has to re-find the line start eleven times in the one paragraph on this page that is meant to be read rather than scanned — and it is the paragraph carrying the claim that none of these values exist on any network. The Status reason line two rows above it is flush-left, so the pane already uses two paragraph alignments and gives the wrong one to the longer block.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER (y≈655–700) and TARGET (y≈726–780) rows
findings.finding: Both 66-character hashes are hard-wrapped into the ~17-character right-aligned value column and run to three lines each, with the third line holding two characters — `32` and `4c` — alone. The breaks fall mid-byte, and a two-character orphan right-aligned under a full line reads as a stray value rather than the tail of the one above. Two rows up, the same pane truncates a hash at a byte boundary with a middle ellipsis (`0xb636167a…66d46359`), and the identity bar does the same; this column is the only place on the page that wraps instead, and it is the least readable of the three treatments.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, line 29 (⊘), line 32 (⊙), and lines 26/27/28/31/34/37/40 (·)
findings.finding: Three execution states are carried by three marks in a 12px-wide gutter column: a ring with a diagonal, a ring with a dot, and a middot. At the rendered size the two rings are ~7px across and differ only in a one-pixel interior feature, so "this arm ran" and "this arm did not run" — the distinction the pane exists to draw — are not separable without zooming. The third state reads better than the other two only because a middot has a different silhouette. The one ⊙ on the page also sits on the current line, whose cyan band and teal rail already dominate it, so the ran-marker has no legible instance at all. Silhouette-level differences (filled versus hollow) would carry this where interior detail does not.

findings.location: Code pane, the `+3` chip under line 26 (y≈243), the `+2` under line 48 (y≈778) and the `+3` under line 49 (y≈822)
findings.finding: When the inline value chips overflow the pane width, the overflow counter drops onto a half-height line of its own beneath the code line, right-aligned to the fade edge. The listing's line rhythm breaks where it does: the 26→27 baseline gap is roughly twice the 34→35 gap, and the same happens twice more at 48 and 49, so the lower third of the pane has three irregular row heights. In a listing whose whole value is that line N is a countable distance from line M, uneven leading is a real cost, and the chip that causes it carries the least information on the row.

findings.location: Code pane header stack, second strip — "LOOP iterate_asteroids line 4 Iteration 3 of 8" (y≈100–130)
findings.finding: `Iteration 3 of 8` is set larger and darker than the pane title `CODE` directly above it, so the sub-header outranks the pane it belongs to. The strip also runs four treatments at nearly one size — a tracked all-caps label, a monospace identifier, an underlined link and a body-face count — with nothing in the type saying which is label, which is subject and which is position.

findings.location: Values pane, `masses` row (y≈672–706)
findings.finding: The eight-element array wraps and leaves `14]` alone on a second right-aligned line, directly above the `masses[2]` row. Two adjacent lines therefore both look like short scalar values in the value column, and the closing bracket is the only cue that one is a continuation. A truncated array with a count — the pane already shows `[Field; 8]` in the type column — would read better than a two-line wrap at this measure.

findings.location: Call Trace region (x691–1144, y68–561) — the area below the "By call order. / Self cost" footer row
findings.finding: The region's last ink is at y320; the pane ends at y561. That is 241px of empty white, 49% of the region's 494px height and 27% of the viewport height, in the middle of the layout. The Values pane below it is not the pane asking for that space either — its eleven rows end at y860 against a pane bottom of y895, so it fits with 35px to spare. The column that is actually short of room is the Code pane, which clips a half row of line 52 at y887–895 and fades out the right end of lines 26, 40, 41, 42, 43, 48 and 49. As drawn, the emptiest area on the page is adjacent to the only pane clipping content in both axes, and the split is fixed rather than responsive to either.

findings.location: Identity bar, x370–933 — the four stepping button groups, the scrubber and the position readout
findings.finding: Measured gaps across that span are 16, 16, 16, 16, 16 and 11px: between step-back/forward and step-in/out, between step-in/out and the frame jumps, between those and the ends-of-trace pair, between the last button group and the scrubber, and between the scrubber and `128`. Six objects of three different kinds are separated by one distance, so proximity does no grouping work at all and the bar reads as a strip of unrelated buttons with a bar and a number stuck on the end. The bar can clearly group when it wants to — the identity cluster on the left uses 8–9px internally with a rule and 24px after it, and the phase rail gets 25px — which makes the flat 16px run in the middle look unconsidered rather than intentional.

The listing's baseline pitch is 23px for twenty-three of its twenty-six rows. Three rows are 44px because the `+3` / `+2` overflow chip cannot fit beside the code and drops onto a half-height line of its own, right-aligned at x613–637 where it aligns with nothing — not the code's left indent, not the value chips it summarises, not the pane's right edge. The result is three double-height gaps scattered down the pane, which in a numbered listing is the one place an irregular vertical rhythm is actively misleading: the eye reads distance between line numbers as distance in the file.

findings.location: Code pane, notice row at y165–205 — the word "in" at the end of the first line (x≈645–664)
findings.finding: The right-edge fade that signals horizontal overflow of the code is painted over the whole pane body, including the wrapped notice above it. The notice does not overflow — it wraps normally to "this window." on the second line — but its first line's last word is dimmed to roughly the fade's midpoint, so the sentence reads as though it has been cut off. An overflow affordance applied to content that does not overflow is worse than no affordance: it makes a complete sentence look truncated and, by the same token, weakens the signal on the seven code lines that really are cut.

findings.location: Three-column split — Transaction pane at x1149–1435 (287px) versus Code at 683px
findings.finding: At this viewport the pane squeezed hardest is the one whose content has the highest minimum width. The Transaction pane's value column is about 17 characters wide, which forces both 66-character hashes (FEE PAYER y655–700, TARGET y726–780) to wrap onto three lines with a two-character orphan on the third, and forces the DATA paragraph into eleven lines. The Call Trace column beside it, at 454px, is showing seven frames whose longest row ends 10px short of its own right edge and has 241px of empty height. Width was taken from the pane that could not give it and left with the pane that did not need it.

findings.location: Left content edges — Call Trace pane (tab label x700, FRAME header x702, frame rows x706) and identity bar (x24) versus pane titles (x13)
findings.finding: Four left edges stack in the Call Trace pane at 700, 702 and 706, differences of 2px and 4px that are too small to read as an intentional indent and too large to look flush; the Values pane repeats it at 700 versus 703. The Transaction pane, by contrast, aligns its title and every row label at exactly 1158. Separately, the identity bar insets its content 24px from the page edge on both sides while every pane insets its title 9px, so the top strip's left and right edges sit visibly inside the grid they head.

findings.location: Code pane, bottom edge at y887–895 — line 52
findings.finding: The last row is bisected by the pane's bottom border: the numerals of `52` are cut through the middle, with no scrollbar or fade at the bottom edge to say that more follows. A half-row at the foot of a scroll container is a normal editor convention, but here it is the only edge of the pane with no overflow signal at all — the right edge has a fade, this one has nothing — so the pane appears to end mid-glyph by accident.

findings.location: Identity bar scrubber (x691–832, y28–34) versus the iteration chips in the Code pane header (chips 1 and 2, x370–450, y90–118)
findings.finding: One grey, #919191, carries opposite meanings in two position widgets 60px apart. On the scrubber it is the unplayed remainder — the elapsed part is #155e75 teal. On the iteration chips it is the fill for iterations 1 and 2, which are the ones already executed, with the not-yet-reached chips 4–8 left unfilled. So a reader who learns "grey means behind you" from the chips reads the scrubber backwards, and vice versa. The teal family is used consistently for position everywhere else on the page (scrubber fill, current-line rail #0e7490, call-trace selection rail #164e63, the numeral and underline of active chip 3 at #164e63), which makes the grey fill on chips 1–2 the single element out of step with the page's own convention.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row badge `Synthetic demo data` (x1273–1426, y215–242) and identity bar phase rail chip `FETCHING` (x959–1035, y18–44)
findings.finding: Both are painted #1e40af on #dbeafe — not a family resemblance, the same two values. One is a permanent statement about what all the data on this page is; the other is a transient engine phase that changes as the session loads. The blue does not contradict the provenance label, so this is not a mislabelled tone, but it does mean the page's most load-bearing badge is toned identically to its most ephemeral status chip, and the two are visible simultaneously at opposite corners. The tone that says 'this is synthetic' should not be recoverable from the tone that says 'currently fetching'.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge x≈648–686 across lines 26, 40, 41, 42, 43, 48 and 49; and the notice row's last word "in" at x≈645–664, y168–184
findings.finding: The horizontal-overflow fade drives real characters below the contrast floor rather than clipping them. Measured across line 42, the literal `100` runs #8146de at 5.43:1 down to #be9fee at 2.24:1 within one token; line 26's tail reaches 1.80:1 and line 48's 1.67:1. Characters at 1.6–2.9:1 are present enough to look like content and too weak to read, which is the worst of both. It also lands on content that does not overflow at all: the notice wraps normally to "this window." on its second line, yet its last word `in` is faded to #e7e7e7 — 1.24:1 — so a complete sentence reads as truncated. Not filed as P1 because the fade is a deliberate overflow signal and the sentence survives without the word, but the ramp needs to stop at a readable value or start further right.

findings.location: Code pane header, iteration chips 4–8 (x480–680, y90–118)
findings.finding: The not-yet-reached chips set their numerals in #727272 on the header's #dddddd fill — 3.54:1, under the 4.5:1 floor for text this size, and these numerals are about 11px. They are the only unvisited-state control on the page and they are also the smallest text in the header strip. Chips 1 and 2 manage 4.93:1 (#242424 on #919191) and the active chip 3 is fine, so the failing state is specifically the one a reader scans to answer "how many iterations are left".

findings.location: Code pane gutter — the ⊙ mark on line 32 (x≈84–92, y376–388) and the ⊘ mark on line 29 (y306–318)
findings.finding: The two branch-arm states are carried by marks that both sit under the contrast floor. The did-not-run ⊘ is #787878 on white: 4.42:1. The did-run ⊙ is #43a1b6 on the #a5f3fc current-line band: 2.40:1 — and that is the only instance of the ran-state on the page, so the state with the most to prove is the least visible mark in the pane. Their accompanying rails do better (#484848 and #0e7490 at x7–8) but are 2px wide and 23px tall, and the rails are the only part of the encoding that clears the floor.

findings.location: Identity bar, phase rail (x959–1202) and the eight stepping buttons (x370–656)
findings.finding: `FETCHING` is toned as the live phase — filled #dbeafe with #1e40af text — while `OPENING` and `POSITIONING` sit at #565656 on white. Everything else on the page is toned as a finished, positioned session: eleven resolved values, a highlighted current line, a call trace with costs. None of the eight stepping buttons carries a disabled or pending tone; all eight use the same #101010 glyph on white. So the one element coloured as in-progress is contradicted by every other element's colour, and a reader cannot tell from the palette whether the controls are live.

findings.location: Values pane changed rows (#854d0e text and left rail at x693, rows `remaining_shield` y622 and `damage` y790) versus the `Partial` badge (#9a3412 on #ffedd5) in the identity bar and Transaction pane
findings.finding: The warm family carries two unrelated meanings: 'this value changed at this step' in the Values pane and the code pane's `damage: 0→2000` chip, and 'the transaction only partly succeeded' in the two Partial badges. The hues differ enough (#854d0e amber-brown versus #9a3412 orange-red) that a careful reader will separate them, and their shapes differ — bare text with a rail versus a filled pill — so this is a nitpick rather than a role collision. But it is the one warm family on an otherwise teal-and-grey page, and it spends its salience on two things at once.

findings.location: Call Trace region, x691–1144, below the "By call order. / Self cost" row at y320 down to the pane edge at y561
findings.finding: 241px empty — 49% of the region, 27% of the viewport height — while the fixture's seven frames occupy the first 190px. At the region's own 25px row pitch that void is room for nine or ten more frames, and the Values pane beneath it is the pane that in a real trace grows without bound: eleven values here, ending 35px short of its own bottom. The region that holds a bounded, shallow structure was given three fifths of the column; the one that holds an unbounded list was given two fifths. At realistic volume — a forty-frame trace with sixty values in scope — this split starves the wrong pane, and nothing in the layout suggests it would rebalance.

findings.location: Code pane, y68–210 — the four stacked header rows above line 26
findings.finding: 142px, 17% of the pane's 828px height, goes to chrome before a single line of code: the `CODE` title bar (25px), the loop/iteration strip (28px), the file tab row (26px) and the "Showing from line 26 …" notice (~45px, two lines). At the pane's own 23px line pitch that is six lines of source. The notice is the most expendable of the four — it states in a full sentence what the line numbers starting at 26 already say — and the file tab row duplicates the filename already shown in every call-trace row. In a register where density is the virtue, the flagship pane opens with four bands of furniture.

findings.location: Code pane body, y210–895 — line pitch
findings.finding: The listing runs at a 23px pitch for glyphs 10px tall, which is 2.3× the cap height where a dense tool listing runs 1.5–1.6×. 26 lines are shown in 685px of body; at 18px rows the same space carries 38, and the type would not change size. The rows are legible — the extra height is not buying legibility, it is buying nothing — and the pane is simultaneously clipping the file at line 52 (a half row at the bottom edge) and fading out the right end of seven lines. The pane is short of space in both axes and is spending a third of the space it has on leading.

findings.location: Transaction pane, bottom edge — `EXECUTIONS` group at y845–893 against the pane border at y895
findings.finding: The pane's content runs flush into its bottom border with no scrollbar, fade or count to say whether anything follows. It matters here because the pane contradicts itself: the Status reason at y180–205 reads `private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded`, naming two executions, and the EXECUTIONS group at the foot lists exactly one — `private`, marked `Not observable`. Either the public entry is below the fold, in which case the drop is unsignalled, or it is absent, in which case the group is incomplete. At this viewport the reader cannot tell which, and this is the pane the register relies on for 'what am I looking at'.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — the badge and paragraph at y215–555
findings.finding: The provenance row occupies 340px of the pane's 828px, 41%, of which 310px is the eleven-line paragraph. The fair question the change invites is whether the row has become too quiet; at this viewport the answer is the reverse — it is the largest single allocation of space on the page, larger than the entire Values pane's content, and it forced the pane's actual data into a 17-character column that wraps both addresses onto three lines. The band's cost was relocated into the pane rather than removed. The badge alone, with the sentences behind a disclosure or set at the pane's foot, would carry the same claim at a fifth of the height.

findings.location: Values pane, type column at x1109–1134 — nine rows reading `Field`
findings.finding: The rightmost column repeats the same four-letter type on nine of eleven rows, at the same size and weight as the values, for a constant that carries no per-row information. The two rows where the type differs (`[Field; 8]` on `masses`, `u32` on `i`) are the only informative cells in the column, and they are the two hardest to spot because they sit in a column of identical strings. Dimming the repeated type, or showing it only where it changes, returns roughly 25px of width to the value column in the pane that most needs it.

findings.location: Whole page — every accent colour: code tokens in the Code pane, the cyan current-line band and its rails, the badges in the identity bar and Transaction pane, the link colour
findings.finding: Sampled, the accents are stock framework defaults, not this product's: #1d4ed8, #1e40af, #dbeafe, #4f46e5, #a5f3fc, #0e7490, #155e75, #164e63, #9a3412, #ffedd5, #854d0e, #166534, #713f12 are all Tailwind palette entries at their published values. The neutral ramp (#ececeb, #dddddd, #919191, #565656, #242424) is warm and clearly custom, so the page is a bespoke greyscale wearing an off-the-shelf colour set. The consequence for this register is concrete: a CodeTracer desktop user recognises this screen by its layout and its pane names, and by nothing in its hue family — the editor tokens in particular are a generic web highlighter's blue/purple/green/brown rather than the product lineage's editor palette, which §3 names as the one thing that must look like CodeTracer wherever it appears.

findings.location: Identity bar, the eight stepping buttons at x370–656
findings.finding: Eight icon-only buttons, no labels and no key hints anywhere in the bar. The desktop application this register must be continuous with names its stepping commands and shows their bindings; here the only way to tell `↖ ↘` (step out / step in) from `|← →|` (previous / next frame) is to recognise two arrow idioms that differ by a stem, and nothing indicates that stepping has a keyboard at all. Reverse stepping is the product's premise and it is the leftmost solid triangle — visible, correctly placed, correctly grouped in a segmented pair — but unnamed. The grouping into four pairs is good and should stay; what is missing is any surface that says what a pair does.

findings.location: Transaction pane — the pills on the CANONICAL (`Yes`, y583–611), FINALITY (`Safe`, y615–647), EXECUTIONS (`Not observable`, y860–884), DATA (`Synthetic demo data`, y215–242) rows and the `Partial` badge at y100–125
findings.finding: Five rows of this pane are dominated by the explorer register's badge primitive at the explorer register's scale: 24–28px pills with 10–12px of horizontal padding and a full-radius outline, carrying one word each. In a pane whose rows are otherwise 25–32px of dense mono, a one-word value styled as a marketing pill outranks the four-line address two rows above it. The desktop app states such facts as text in the value column. The pill is the right component in the explorer's transaction page and reads as an unconsidered carry-over here, where the same information as plain toned text would fit the pane's own density.

findings.location: Code pane header, the iteration chips 1–8 at x370–680, y90–118
findings.finding: Eight numbered chips in a row read as the explorer's pagination control rather than as a loop-iteration stepper: same pill shape, same numeric sequence, same left-to-right progression. The distinction that matters here — which iterations have run, which is current, which are ahead — is carried only by fill and an underline, so the crossing reads as a component borrowed rather than a tool control designed. It is also the only place on the page where a control implies a jump target without saying what jumping does to the session position.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the line `Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded` at y180–205
findings.finding: A serialised enum value is printed verbatim in a pane that otherwise writes in sentences, two rows above a paragraph that is carefully composed English. The hyphenated identifier is honest and unambiguous — a virtue — but it is the machine's spelling, not the product's voice, and it sits in the most prominent third of the pane. `Private part succeeded; public part succeeded` carries the same fact in the register's own tone.

findings.location: Identity bar, right-hand actions at x1356–1415 versus the stepping groups at x370–656
findings.finding: Two button vocabularies share a 64px bar: the share and download actions are near-circular 34px squircles standing alone, while the eight controls are 28px segmented rectangles at a small radius. Both are defensible in isolation and their functions do differ, but the radius jump is large enough that the two right-hand buttons read as belonging to a different application than the eight on the left.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the `DATA` row — the nine-line paragraph beneath the `Synthetic demo data` badge, occupying x≈1636–1908, y≈228–412
findings.finding: The provenance sentences are right-aligned. Nine consecutive lines of prose with a ragged LEFT edge is the slowest setting continuous text can be given, because the eye has to re-find every line start, and the sawtooth here runs to about 30 px. It is inconsistent with its own pane — `aztec private function executed client-side; only proofs, nullifiers and commitments are published` and `This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds` are both left-aligned and both span the pane — so the rule is not 'prose is right-aligned here', it is that this paragraph was dropped into the label/value grid's value column and took its alignment. The same mistake costs width: the block is confined to a 275 px column with the label gutter empty beside all nine lines, which is why it needs nine. This is the weakest element because it is the element this round created. The band was removed on the argument that provenance should be read rather than stepped over; what replaced it is the least readable text on the page, carrying the page's most important claim, and the fix costs nothing and removes no information.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — the provenance paragraph beginning "Every block, transaction, address and hash…"
findings.finding: The provenance sentences are set flush-right, ragged-left, over eight lines, because the row inherits the value column's right alignment. The two other prose blocks in the same pane — the EXECUTIONS note ("aztec private function executed client-side…") and the SELECTOR note ("This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds…") — are both flush-left. So the pane uses two paragraph alignments, and the flush-right one is the longest block and the one carrying the honesty claim. Eight ragged line-starts is the worst case for a paragraph a reader is meant to actually read rather than scan.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows
findings.finding: Both 40-hex addresses wrap onto a second right-aligned line at an arbitrary character (…e2a272b5 / e430d5d932), splitting a byte across the line break. Everywhere else on the page a long value is truncated with a middle ellipsis at a byte boundary (0xb63616…6359 in the identity bar, 0xb636167a…66d46359 in this same pane, two rows up). Two different strategies for the same data type in one pane, and the wrapping one produces a second line that is neither a full value nor a recognisable tail.

findings.location: Code pane, gutter marks at line 29 (⊘) and line 32 (⊙)
findings.finding: The two branch-arm glyphs render at roughly 10px as rings of the same diameter, weight and colour; the entire semantic difference between "this arm did not run" and "this arm did run" is a 1–2px interior feature (a diagonal stroke versus a dot). The three states do read as one family — all three occupy the same gutter column at the same optical size, and absence-of-mark is a legible third state — but the family's two marked members are not reliably told apart at the size they are set. A shape difference at the silhouette level (ring versus filled, or a differing rail weight) would carry it; an interior detail at 10px does not.

findings.location: Call Trace pane, column header row — "FRAME" and "ACIR opcodes"
findings.finding: One header row sets its two labels in two casings: FRAME is tracked all-caps matching the pane titles, ACIR opcodes is a caps acronym followed by lowercase. Whatever the reason (an acronym plus a noun), the effect is that the right-hand header does not read as the same level as the left-hand one, in the only row on the page where two headers sit side by side.

findings.location: Transaction pane, first two lines — the `Partial 0xb636167a…66d46359` badge row and the full hash directly beneath it
findings.finding: A middle-truncated hash is set immediately above the full hash it truncates, and the truncated one is the larger, more prominent of the two. The truncation therefore buys nothing here — the reader gets both forms in adjacent lines, and the pane spends its most prominent line on the less informative one.

findings.location: Code pane, second header strip — "LOOP iterate_asteroids line 4 Iteration 3 of 8"
findings.finding: One strip carries four type treatments at near-identical size: an all-caps label (LOOP), a monospace identifier, a link (line 4) and a body-face count (Iteration 3 of 8). Nothing in the type says which of these is the label, which is the subject and which is the position within it; the strip reads left-to-right as four peers. The iteration chips 1–8 below it, where the active 3 is underlined, do the same job far more clearly.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row label
findings.finding: The provenance row's label is set identically to BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER and the rest — same size, tracking, weight and emphasis. Nothing in the type marks it as the row that says what all the other rows are. Its eight-line paragraph does give it more area than any other row, so the claim is not lost; but the row is prominent by accident of content length rather than by any typographic decision, and a shorter producer statement would make it vanish into the list. Raising the DATA label one emphasis level would make the prominence intentional.

findings.location: Amber/orange: the `Partial` badge in the identity bar and again in the Transaction pane header, versus the `damage: 0→2000` chip at code line 32 and the values `9000` and `2000` in the Values pane
findings.finding: One hue carries two unrelated roles. Amber marks trace completeness on the two `Partial` badges, and amber marks changed-at-this-step on the inline chip at line 32 and on the two amber numerals in the Values pane. The changed-value role is otherwise the best colour work on the page — it is consistent across Code and Values, so one glance connects the chip to the row. But sharing its hue with a completeness badge means the reader has to use position, not colour, to know which claim is being made, and the two badges are at the top of the same eye path.

findings.location: Cyan: `line 4` and `Self cost` and `101:0` (links); the `src/shield.nr` tab underline and the iteration-3 chip underline (active); `FETCHING` in the phase rail (active phase); the scrubber's filled portion
findings.finding: One accent hue does four jobs. Three of them — link, active selection, progress fill — can defensibly share an accent in a tool. The fourth cannot: `FETCHING` in the phase rail is set in the same cyan as `line 4`, which is a link sixty pixels below it in the next pane, so a non-interactive status word is styled exactly like the page's interactive text. The phase rail is the element the register relies on to be read as honest reporting rather than as something to click.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, the `⊘` at line 29 and the `⊙` at line 32, against the `·` statement markers on every other line in the same column
findings.finding: The new three-state branch family is carried entirely by glyph shape with no colour support. Both marks read as the same neutral grey, and that grey is close to the inert `·` markers sharing the column, so the two states that carry meaning are not tonally separated from each other or from the decoration around them. This is the one place on the page where a state distinction gets no colour, in a theme that colours changed values, active phases, selected frames and trace completeness. A dim/normal tonal pair — did-not-run recessed, did-run at full emphasis — would make the family read at a glance and would also cover the case where the glyph itself is too small to resolve.

findings.location: Transaction pane, EXECUTIONS row — the `Not observable` badge on the `private` line and the `Trace ready` badge on the `public` line; compare `Synthetic demo data` (DATA), `Partial`, `Yes` (CANONICAL) and `Safe` (FINALITY)
findings.finding: Badge fill versus outline encodes nothing consistent. `Not observable` and `Trace ready` are direct peers — the two halves of one execution split, two lines apart — and one is an outline grey chip while the other is a filled green one. Elsewhere `Synthetic demo data` is filled, `Partial` is outline amber, and `Yes` and `Safe` are outline grey. So the page has four badge treatments and no rule mapping treatment to meaning; a reader cannot learn that filled means anything, which wastes the strongest contrast tool the palette has.

findings.location: The dim-grey band: inactive file tabs `Nargo.toml` / `Prover.toml` / `src/main.nr`; iteration chips 4–8; `OPENING` and `POSITIONING` in the phase rail
findings.finding: One very low-emphasis grey is used for three different kinds of de-emphasis at 10–11px — inactive-but-clickable (the file tabs), not-yet-reached (chips 4–8, which also differ from chips 1–2 only by this same opacity, so past-versus-future is carried by contrast alone), and pending phase (OPENING, POSITIONING). All three sit near the bottom of the contrast range on near-black. The phase names are the worst case: they are what tells the reader what happens after FETCHING, and they are set at the emphasis level the page otherwise reserves for inert decoration. Density is not the issue — one step up in luminance costs nothing.

findings.location: Code pane, line 32 — the left rail and row highlight on the current position, versus the left rail on line 29
findings.finding: Line 32 is simultaneously the current position and a branch arm that ran, and both facts are drawn at the pane's left edge in the same treatment family, so nothing in the colour separates 'you are here' from 'this arm executed'. Line 29 carries a rail too, which confirms the rail is the branch signal rather than the position signal — but only by inference from a second row. The position itself is not in doubt (the row band and the value chips carry it), which is why this is a nitpick and not a B5 failure; the ambiguity is about which of the two signals the rail belongs to.

findings.location: Code pane, line 40 (`initial_shield:Field, remaining_shield:Field`) against the comments at lines 41 and 56
findings.finding: The type green and the comment green sit close enough in hue and luminance that on line 40, where four `Field` annotations trail the parameter names, the type colour reads at first glance as the start of a trailing comment — particularly with the actual comment on line 41 directly beneath it in a very similar green. The editor palette is legitimately inherited here, so this is a preference rather than a defect, but widening the separation between the comment and type tokens is cheap.

findings.location: Pane boundaries between the Code pane, the Call Trace/Values column and the Transaction pane
findings.finding: Pane body surfaces sit only a few percent above the page background, so nearly all pane separation is done by the header strips — which are a clearer step up — plus a hairline border. It holds at 1920 because the three columns are wide and the headers align, but the Values pane's lower half and the empty region under the call trace read as page background rather than as pane interiors, which makes both look like gaps in the layout rather than panes with room left.

findings.location: Middle column — the Call Trace region below the `By call order · Self cost` footer, y≈322 to the region border at y≈670
findings.finding: This is the measurement the round asked for. The tabbed region occupies 604 px of the 1012 px column (60%); its seven frames run y≈125–305 and its footer ends at y≈320, so ~348 px — 57% of the region, 34% of the whole column — is blank pane. Meanwhile the Values pane below it ends at y≈945 with a further ~130 px of slack, and the Transaction pane in the next column is clipped mid-object inside the RAW (chain-native) block at the viewport floor. Two panes on this screen are showing less than they hold and the third is showing nothing at all in a third of a metre of column. The height belongs to whichever pane is truncated; on this fixture that is Values and Transaction, not Call Trace. The proportion should follow content, or the region should keep a fixed frame count and hand the remainder down.

findings.location: Code pane header, the iteration chip row — chips `1`–`8` beside `Iteration 3 of 8`
findings.finding: The chip fills for iterations 1–3 are #727272 and the numerals on them are ~13 px: white #dddddd on 1 and 2 gives 3.5:1, and the current chip's cyan #67e8f9 numeral gives 3.3:1. Both are under the 4.5:1 floor for text this size, and the worst of the two is the one that states where in the loop the session is. Chips 4–8 (grey on #202020) are fine. This is the row that carries loop position — the only place `3 of 8` is expressed as something clickable — so it is the wrong row to have the page's lowest text contrast. Darkening the ran-chip fill or setting the numerals white would fix it without changing density.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the `DATA` row — the nine-line paragraph beginning `Every block, transaction, address and` and ending `published under.`
findings.finding: The provenance sentences are right-aligned. Nine lines of body prose with a ragged LEFT edge is the slowest possible setting for continuous text, because every line start has to be re-found. It is also inconsistent inside its own pane: the two other explanatory paragraphs — `aztec private function executed client-side…` under EXECUTIONS and `This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds…` under DECODED INPUT — are left-aligned and full-width. The alignment is inherited from the label/value grid this row sits in, where right-aligned values are correct for `Yes`, `Safe` and hashes; prose is not a value and should break out of that column. This is the element the band was removed in favour of, so it is the one that most needs to read cleanly.

findings.location: Code pane, the listing body y≈190–1075 — lines 26 to 61
findings.finding: The pane now runs the full height and shows 36 lines in ~890 px: a 23 px pitch on 13 px monospace, about 1.8 line-height. The rows are legible — that part of the change works — but the reclaimed height bought eight more rows rather than a denser listing, and inline value chips (`damage: 0→2000`, `+3`, `result=90`) already force extra leading on the rows that carry them, so uniform 23 px pays that cost on the 30 rows that do not. A 19–20 px base pitch with chip rows allowed to grow would show roughly eight further lines at the same legibility.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, x≈74–84 — the `⊘` at line 29, the `⊙` at line 32, and the statement dots on lines 26–28, 31, 34, 37, 40, 42–44, 46, 48–50, 53–54, 56–58, 60–61
findings.finding: The two branch glyphs do read as one family: same column, same ~9 px ring, each with its own left rail. They are separable at this size, but mostly by hue and rail colour (grey #919191 versus cyan #06b6d4) rather than by shape — the slash and the centre dot differ by about two pixels of ink, so at 100% a greyscale reader is distinguishing them on the rail alone. The third mark in that column is a different problem: the ordinary-line `·` peaks at a single cyan pixel per row, so a mark that appears on twenty lines is effectively invisible while the two that appear once each are the loudest things in the gutter. Nothing on the page names any of the three, so a reader learns the family by inference.

findings.location: Code pane right edge, x≈916 — lines 40 (`…shield_regen_perce`) and 53 (`…damage: Field,`)
findings.finding: Long lines are cut hard at the pane edge, mid-identifier, with no ellipsis, no fade and no visible horizontal scrollbar, so nothing indicates whether the rest of the signature exists or the pane simply ends. Clipping inside a code viewport is normal for this register and the fix must not be to wrap or to narrow the listing; a fade or a scroll affordance at the edge is enough to say the content continues.

findings.location: Transaction pane, second line under the full hash — `Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded`, wrapping onto a second line above the `DATA` row
findings.finding: A raw internal enum is printed verbatim as human-facing copy. Everything else this product says is written: `aztec private function executed client-side; only proofs, nullifiers and commitments are published — no call structure to trace` and `This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds…` are sentences with a subject and a claim. This one is a hyphen-joined identifier that wraps mid-token and restates in machine vocabulary what the `Partial` badge two lines above already says. It also breaks the pane's own row primitive: every other fact here is a grey letterspaced label in the left column with its value at the right, and this is an inline `Label:` prefix in flowing text. Copy is a design property in this register, and this is the one place on the page where the seam between the model and the surface shows.

findings.location: Identity bar, x≈670–1462 — scrubber, then `Engine loading — 18 MB`, then `128 / 1315`, then the `FETCHING | OPENING | POSITIONING` rail; empty bar from x≈1462 to `NOIR` at x≈1799
findings.finding: The bar reads as two halves with different rules. The left half is grouped and desktop-like: identity cluster, a vertical divider, then four boxed control pairs. The right half is four unlike objects with no dividers, no shared container and no consistent idiom — a bare progress-bar shape, a sans sentence, a mono fraction, and a segmented pill. Two of them say the same thing: `Engine loading — 18 MB` and the phase rail both report engine load, one as prose and one as a segmented control, side by side. Worse, the trace scrubber is placed immediately to the left of that sentence, so the page's only position-in-trace element sits against the words `Engine loading` with an 8% cyan fill and reads as the download's progress bar; the `128 / 1315` that would disambiguate it is on the far side of the sentence. There is 337 px of empty bar to the right of the rail, so the grouping is not forced by space.

findings.location: Transaction pane — `Yes` (CANONICAL) and `Safe` (FINALITY) against `Partial`, `Trace ready`, `Not observable` and `Synthetic demo data`
findings.finding: One pill primitive carries three different kinds of content. It is a status on `Partial` and `Trace ready`, a provenance claim on `Synthetic demo data`, and a plain field value on `Yes` and `Safe`. A boolean answer wearing the same chrome as a trace-availability state teaches the reader that the pill means nothing in particular, which weakens the two places where it is load-bearing. `Yes` and `Safe` would read as facts if they were simply set as values in the right column like the hashes and `88000 / 200000 mana`.

findings.location: Code pane header — the file tabs (`src/shield.nr` active), the `CALL TRACE` tab in the next column, and iteration chip `3` in the same header row
findings.finding: Three drawings of 'active' appear within a hundred pixels of each other: the file tab is white text with a white underline, the region tab is white text with a white underline, and the current iteration chip is a filled chip with cyan text and a cyan underline. The first two agree, which makes the third look like a different concept rather than the same one in a different container. The data panes get this right — the current line in Code and the current frame in Call Trace share one cyan rail and row fill — so the divergence is confined to the header vocabulary and is cheap to reconcile by giving the chip the same accent as its neighbours or the tabs the same accent as the chip.

findings.location: Register crossings — `line 4` in the Code pane header, `Self cost` in the call trace footer, `101:0` in the Transaction pane's BLOCK row
findings.finding: Three underlined periwinkle web links appear inside the tool. The brief sanctions one crossing into this register — the editor tokens — and that one is used well. These are a second, unstated crossing: the desktop app expresses navigation targets as selectable rows and affordances, not as underlined hypertext, so these read as the explorer's link primitive carried in rather than as a decision. `101:0` is defensible because it genuinely leaves for a chain page, but `Self cost` toggles a column and `line 4` moves the listing, and neither is a document link.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge (~x=917) at lines 40, 48 and 53
findings.finding: Three source lines are cut at the pane's right edge mid-identifier — line 40 ends at "shield_regen_perce", line 53 ends at "damage: Field, r". There is no horizontal scrollbar, no fade, no wrap glyph and no ellipsis, so nothing on screen says the line continues. This is the widest pane on the page (roughly 47% of the viewport) and it is the only one whose primary content is being cut, while the two narrower columns beside it both have vertical slack. Either the pane needs a visible overflow affordance or the column split needs to move width toward it.

findings.location: Call Trace tabbed region, area below the "By call order. / Self cost" footer
findings.finding: The tabbed region runs about 600px tall. Its content — header row, seven frames, footer — ends roughly 250px in, leaving about 340px (≈57% of the region) empty. The Values pane below it holds ten rows and ends about 125px short of the viewport, so the column as a whole carries roughly 470px of void out of about 1010px. Nothing in either pane is scrolled, so no reallocation between them recovers anything; the measurement the brief asks for is that at this fixture volume the whole middle column is under half full, and the height it is holding is height the Code pane cannot borrow because it is in another column.

findings.location: Identity bar, from the stepping cluster (~x=375) to the phase rail (~x=1478)
findings.finding: The bar reads as a strip of objects rather than as grouped clusters. The gaps separating the three stepping sub-groups (◀▶ / |← →| / |←← →→|) are close in size to the gap between the last stepping group and the scrubber, and to the gaps between "Engine loading — 18 MB", the "128 / 1315" readout and the FETCHING·OPENING·POSITIONING rail. So a status string, a position readout and a phase rail — three unrelated objects — sit at the same proximity as two halves of one control cluster. The only gap that does group anything is the ~320px void before the right-hand actions.

findings.location: Identity bar, scrubber (~x=675–935) and the empty span from the phase rail to the NOIR badge (~x=1490–1795)
findings.finding: The scrubber is about 260px wide and expresses a position of 128 in 1315 steps — roughly five steps per pixel, and a filled portion about 22px long. Immediately to its right the bar holds about 320px of nothing before the right-hand actions. The one element on the page whose usefulness scales directly with its length is the shortest thing in its row, and the dead space that would more than double it is nine pixels of gap away in the same container.

findings.location: Transaction pane, label/value grid — DATA, EXECUTIONS and SELECTOR rows compared with BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY
findings.finding: One grid runs three alignment regimes. Short values (Yes, Safe, 101:0, 88000 / 200000) are right-flush to the pane edge. The DATA provenance paragraph is also right-flush, so its eight lines are ragged on the left. But the EXECUTIONS note and the SELECTOR note break out of the value column entirely and set flush-left from the label column's own left edge, and the `private` / `public` sub-rows put their badges at a third x position that matches neither the label edge nor the value edge. Scanning the pane top to bottom, the reader's eye has no stable edge to return to.

findings.location: Transaction pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) code block at the bottom of the pane
findings.finding: The JSON block's longest line ("contract": "0x1b31c04d5920b0b5936f12…) is cut at the pane's right edge mid-value, and the block also continues below the viewport fold. Neither overflow direction has an affordance — no scrollbar, no fade, no wrap. It is the second instance of the same pattern as the Code pane, and here the clipped content is a hash, where a cut with no ellipsis convention is indistinguishable from a value that simply ends.

findings.location: Code pane, left rail at the pane edge (~x=8) versus the branch glyphs at ~x=78, lines 29 and 32
findings.finding: Each branch-arm mark is drawn as two pieces — a short rail flush against the pane's outer edge and a glyph in the gutter — with the right-aligned line number sitting between them. The two halves of one signal are about 70px apart with an unrelated element in the gap, so the rail reads as pane furniture rather than as part of the mark it belongs to. Moving the rail inboard of the line number, or dropping it in favour of a heavier gutter glyph, would make the mark one object.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows
findings.finding: Most rows in the pane sit on an even ~30px rhythm (BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY). FEE PAYER and TARGET each wrap their address onto a second line and take roughly 50px, so the rhythm breaks twice in the middle of the list and then resumes. Because the wrap is right-aligned, the second line starts at an unpredictable x, which is where the even-rhythm scan visibly stalls.

findings.location: Transaction pane (x1149–1435), the `DATA` row — badge at y215–242 and the sentence block at y245–555, set in the value column
findings.finding: This is the weakest element on the page, and it is weakest precisely because it is the one the page cannot afford to have weak: it is the only place a reader in this register can learn that none of these values exists on any network. Three faults compound. (a) Alignment — eleven lines of prose set flush-right, ragged-left, because the row inherited the value column's alignment. Every line starts at a different x, so the return sweep has no anchor and the block must be laboured through rather than read. Nothing else on this page is set that way, and the same pane proves the alternative two rows up, where `Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded` is flush-left across the full pane width. (b) Measure — about 28 characters, which is what a 287px pane's value column gives you. That measure is also what forces `Every block, transaction,` / `address and hash on this` / `chain is generated from a` to break three times inside one clause, and it is the same constraint that wraps FEE PAYER and TARGET onto three lines each with two-character orphans (`32`, `4c`) at the pane's foot. (c) Cost — 340px including the badge, 41% of the pane's 828px height, more than the eleven rows of the Values pane occupy, in the narrowest column on the page. The band that was removed on 2026-08-31 spent ~190px of full-page width and was named the weakest element by both adversarial reviewers of the previous round; this row spends 340px of the one pane whose content has a hard minimum width. The cost was relocated and increased, not removed, and the reading experience of the claim itself got worse in the move. It is not too quiet — that was the fair question to ask, and the answer at this viewport is the opposite. Set the sentences flush-left across the pane's full width beneath the label and badge and the block falls to roughly five lines, the addresses get their column back, and the claim becomes scannable instead of merely present.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — the paragraph beginning "Every block, transaction, address and hash on this chain is generated from a fixed seed…", y≈245–545
findings.finding: The provenance paragraph is the weakest element on the page because it is simultaneously the largest consumer of space and the hardest thing here to read, and because both faults are consequences of the move that was supposed to fix it. It runs thirteen lines and roughly 325px in a 285px-wide column — 39% of the Transaction pane's 827px, a larger share of its new host than the 17% the band took of the viewport it was removed from. It is set flush-right with a ragged left edge at a ~24-character measure, because the row inherited the pane's label-left/value-right alignment; thirteen unpredictable line-starts is the worst available setting for sentences, and it is the only flush-right prose on the page. Its cost is paid by the rows underneath: BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST·MANA and EXECUTIONS are all pushed into the bottom 40% of the column, and FEE PAYER and TARGET each burn three lines wrapping a hash and end on two-character orphans (`32`, `4c`) as a direct result. The claim itself is right and the `Synthetic demo data` badge carries it well at a glance — so the row is not too quiet. It is too long, in the wrong alignment, in the narrowest column on the screen.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — the paragraph beginning "Every block, transaction, address and hash on this chain…"
findings.finding: The provenance sentences are set flush-right, ragged-left, over thirteen lines at roughly a 24-character measure, because the row inherits the pane's label-left/value-right alignment. Every other paragraph-shaped thing on the page is flush-left (the Code pane's "Showing from line 26…" note, the call trace's "By call order."). A flush-right setting gives the reader thirteen unpredictable line-starts, which is the worst available treatment for the one block on this page that must be read as sentences rather than scanned. At 24 characters the measure is also below the floor at which any paragraph reads well; the wide capture sets the same text in eight lines.

findings.location: Code pane, listing rows 26–27, 48–49 and 49–50
findings.finding: The listing has two row pitches. Plain lines sit on a 23px pitch; lines whose inline value badge does not fit push a `+3`/`+2` chip onto a row of its own and the pitch becomes 41–44px. Line numbers are therefore not an even column, and the vertical scan a reader uses to count lines or to keep the current position in peripheral vision breaks three times in twenty-six rows. A code listing's line-number column is a ruler; a ruler with unequal divisions is not one.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER and TARGET rows
findings.finding: Both 64-character hashes wrap across three right-aligned lines and leave a two-character orphan on the last one — `32` for FEE PAYER, `4c` for TARGET. The identity bar and the pane's own header both truncate with a middle ellipsis (`0xb63616…6359`, `0xb636167a…66d46359`), so the page owns a truncation convention and does not apply it to the two rows that most need it. A three-line wrap ending in two characters reads as a rendering accident rather than a value, and it breaks mid-byte at both wrap points.

findings.location: Values pane, `masses` row
findings.finding: The array value `[100, 2000, 200, 100, 100, 50, 50, 14]` wraps with its continuation `14]` right-aligned on the second line, so the closing bracket sits roughly 400px to the right of where the eye left the sequence and the array appears to read out of order. Continuations of a bracketed sequence should hang to the opening bracket, not to the value column's right edge.

findings.location: Code pane header (file tab `src/shield.nr`, iteration chip `3`) and Call Trace tab strip (`CALL TRACE`)
findings.finding: Three different underline treatments express "current" within 500px of each other: a thick straight rule under `CALL TRACE`, a rounded-ended rule under the active file tab `src/shield.nr`, and a double rule under iteration chip `3`. All three mean the same thing at the same moment. One underline weight and one cap style would let the reader learn the mark once.

findings.location: Values pane, type column — `Field`, `[Field; 8]`, `u32`
findings.finding: The type names are set in the UI sans face while the identifier and value columns either side of them are monospace. `Field`, `u32` and `[Field; 8]` are Noir source identifiers and belong to the code face; setting them in the interface face makes the row read as two documents. It also costs the column its tabular alignment — `[Field; 8]` and `Field` do not share a right edge cleanly.

findings.location: Code pane, the note row "Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window."
findings.finding: The note is set in the code face at code size and at the pane's full ~110-character measure, so it competes with the listing directly beneath it in weight, face and size, and orphans two words ("this window.") on a second line. A note about the listing should be a distinct type level from the listing — smaller, or in the interface face, or held to a measure that fits one line.

findings.location: Code pane header, loop strip `LOOP iterate_asteroids line 4 Iteration 3 of 8`
findings.finding: `Iteration 3 of 8` is the brightest and heaviest run of text anywhere in the Code pane header — heavier than the pane title `CODE` and than the active file tab — while the chip row immediately to its right already states the same fact and states it better, since the chips also carry which iterations have been visited. The loudest type on the header is the most redundant.

findings.location: Middle column — the Call Trace / Event Log tab region (y66–558) and the Values pane below it (y566–893)
findings.finding: The measurement the Watch-for item asks for: the tab region is 492px of the column's 827px (60%). Its content — tab strip, FRAME header, seven frames and the `By call order. / Self cost` footer — ends at y322, leaving 233px empty, 47% of the region. The Values pane gets the remaining 327px, fills it to y860 with ten rows, and has already wrapped the `masses` array onto a second line to fit. So the fixed 60/40 split hands half a region of dead space to the pane that is a third full and squeezes the pane that is overflowing. The split should be content-driven, or the surplus should go to Values; at this fixture the region needs about 260px and Values could use every pixel of the rest.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge at x≈684 — lines 26, 41, 42, 43, 48 and 49
findings.finding: Six lines are cut hard at the pane border in the middle of a token — line 26 ends `…(initial_shield, re`, line 42 ends `…after each h`, line 49 ends `…initial_shield as u` — with no horizontal scrollbar, no fade, no ellipsis and no wrap. Nothing on the page tells the reader that content continues to the right or offers a way to reach it, so a line that is cut is indistinguishable from a line that ends there. Horizontal overflow in a code listing is normal; silently absorbing it at a hairline is not. Not raised to P1 only because the pane is a listing rather than a container leaking content, and the position line 32 is fully visible.

findings.location: Code pane, inline value badges on lines 26, 27, 28, 32, 48, 49 and 50
