findings.finding: The badges have no anchor and no column. `damage=0` sits at x≈325, `shield_pct=90` at x≈350, `damage: 0→2000` at x≈490, `result=90 →90` at x≈290, and the `+3`/`+2` overflow chips are pushed right to x≈612–640 on rows of their own. Three different alignment strategies — trailing the code, floating mid-pane, and flush to the pane's right inset — inside one twenty-six-row listing. The eye cannot form a scan lane for the value overlay, which is the whole reason the overlay exists.

findings.location: Column widths — Transaction pane (285px) against Code pane (680px)
findings.finding: The narrowest column carries the page's widest atoms. The Transaction pane is 285px and must render 64-character hashes (FEE PAYER, TARGET) and a thirteen-line paragraph in it, so both wrap badly; the Code pane has 680px and still clips its lines. At laptop width the Transaction pane is the column that should have taken width from Code, whose listing is left-heavy and whose right third is mostly whitespace between the code and the pane edge on twelve of twenty-six rows.

findings.location: Code pane, bottom edge at y≈888 — line 52
findings.finding: The listing's last row is clipped at roughly half its height, showing the top halves of the glyphs `52`. The pane ends mid-row rather than on a whole one, so the bottom edge reads as a rendering failure rather than a scroll boundary. A listing pane should either round its height to a whole number of rows or mask the partial row.

findings.location: Code pane header stack, y66–202
findings.finding: Four stacked header rows — the `CODE` title, the loop/iteration strip, the file tab row, and the two-line "Showing from line 26…" note — consume 136px before the first line of code at y213, 16% of the pane's 827px height. Three of the four are separated by the same gap, so the stack reads as four peers rather than a title with two subordinate strips; proximity is not doing any grouping here.

findings.location: Values pane, `masses[2]` row beneath `masses`
findings.finding: The child row is indented roughly 8px from its parent `masses` — about half a character of the mono face. At that offset the indentation reads as a misalignment rather than as nesting, especially with no guide rule, while the Call Trace pane two panes above expresses the same relationship with both a clear indent step and a vertical guide. The two panes should use one nesting primitive.

findings.location: Code pane gutter (executed dots on lines 26–50, the `⊙` on line 32, the current-position rail), identity bar scrubber fill and active phase `FETCHING`, Code pane header iteration chip `3`
findings.finding: One cyan (#05B3D0 / #06B6D4, thumb #67E8F9) carries six distinct meanings on this screen: an executed-line dot, the new `⊙` branch-arm-ran marker, the current-position left rail and line number, the scrubber's elapsed fill, the active loading phase, and the current loop iteration. Two of those belong to a coverage family (this ran / this did not) and four to a position family (you are here). Because the current line is the only line carrying `⊙`, and it is also the only line carrying the cyan rail, a reader has no way to learn from this image whether cyan means "ran" or "here" — the page's newest semantic is rendered in the hue least able to carry it. Coverage and position need separate hues.

findings.location: Transaction pane DATA badge (#60A5FA) against the pane's `101:0` link and Call Trace `Self cost` (#818CF8) and the gutter/scrubber cyan (#06B6D4)
findings.finding: Three blues sit within one screen and mean three unrelated things: indigo #818CF8 for navigation (`← aztec`, `line 4`, `101:0`, `Self cost`), cyan for position/coverage, and #60A5FA for the `Synthetic demo data` provenance badge. The provenance badge is the odd one — it is neither a link nor a position, yet it is tonally between two hues that are, so at a glance it reads as another clickable chip. A provenance claim about synthetic data should not borrow the informational-link tone; it needs a role colour of its own, distinct from both.

findings.location: Code pane header, iteration chips 4–8
findings.finding: The unvisited iteration chips render #727272 numerals on a #202020 fill — 3.39:1, below the 4.5:1 floor for normal text, at roughly 11px. These are not a disabled control: they are the future iterations of the loop, and the reader is meant to compare 3-of-8 against how many remain. The tool rubric rewards density but §6 B2 explicitly refuses low-contrast small text as a way of buying it. The visited chips (1, 2) and the current chip clear the floor; only the state that carries the count fails it.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, line 32 — the `⊙` glyph on the selected-row fill
findings.finding: The `⊙` ran-marker is #06B6D4 on the #324155 current-row fill: 4.28:1, below the floor, in a glyph about 7px across whose meaning lives entirely in a 1–2px interior mark that separates it from `⊘`. Its counterpart `⊘` on line 29 sits on the plain #1B1B1B pane surface at 5.47:1, so the two halves of the same new three-state signal are rendered at different contrasts on different surfaces. The state that ran is the one rendered worse.

findings.location: Identity bar, phase rail — `FETCHING` active in cyan, `OPENING` and `POSITIONING` dim
findings.finding: The rail colours the first phase as active while every pane on the page shows a fully positioned session: the readout says step 128 of 1315, the call trace has seven frames, Values has ten resolved values and the Code pane has a current-position highlight. Cyan on `FETCHING` therefore says "still loading" over a surface that says "loaded". The phase rail is a required element and named phases are the right primitive, but the active-state colour has to agree with what the rest of the screen is asserting, or the one honest status indicator on the page is the one thing contradicting it.

findings.location: Page canvas behind and between the panes (#000000) against pane surfaces (#1B1B1B) and hairlines (#565656)
findings.finding: The canvas is pure black while the panes sit at #1B1B1B and their headers at #282828. Pure black is a wider step down than any other in the surface ladder, so the 5px inter-pane gutters read louder than the pane borders they sit beside, and the #565656 hairlines only reach 2.86:1 against the canvas. A dark-grey workspace behind the panes — the desktop app's convention — would let the border weight, rather than the void between panes, carry the structure.

findings.location: Identity bar `Partial` badge and Transaction pane `Partial` badge (#FB923C) against Values pane changed values `9000` and `2000` (#FCD34D) and the amber row rail on `remaining_shield`
findings.finding: Two ambers sit close enough to read as one role while meaning two different things — a transaction status on the badges and a changed-since-previous-step diff mark in the Values pane. They are far enough apart on the page not to be confusing yet, but the diff mark is the one that has to survive a dense pane of similar values, and sharing a family with a status badge costs it distinctiveness. One of the two should move off amber.

findings.location: Middle column, Call Trace region below the `By call order. / Self cost` footer (y322–555)
findings.finding: The measurement the Watch-for item asks for and which had not been taken: the tab region occupies 492px of the column's 827px, its seven frames and footer end at y322, and 233px — 47% of the region — is empty. At the 25px row pitch the pane uses, that void would hold nine more frames. Meanwhile the Values pane beneath it has 327px, fills to y860, and has had to wrap `masses` onto two lines to fit ten values. In a register whose rubric names density a virtue, the fixed split gives half a region of nothing to the pane that is a third full and starves the pane that is overflowing. The Values pane is the one that should have the height at this fixture.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — badge plus the thirteen-line paragraph, y220–545
findings.finding: This is the fair question the move invites, and the honest answer is that the row is not too quiet — it is too expensive. The provenance block runs 325px of the pane's 827px, 39%, which is a larger share of the pane it moved into than the 17% the band cost the viewport it moved out of. It pushes BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST·MANA and EXECUTIONS into the bottom 40% of the column, and TARGET and FEE PAYER each burn three lines wrapping as a result. The badge `Synthetic demo data` already carries the claim at a glance; three sentences at a 24-character measure is the most expensive way to carry the rest. Two lines with the remainder on demand would keep the claim and return roughly 200px to the metadata.

findings.location: Code pane, listing rows 26–52
findings.finding: The listing runs a 23px row pitch on roughly 13px monospace — a line-height near 1.75, against the 1.35–1.45 a desktop debugger uses. Twenty-six source lines are visible in the 690px of listing area; at a 19px pitch it would show thirty-four. This matters more here than usual because the pane's own note says the session's window starts at line 26 and the lines above are not shown, so the reader is already short of context, and eight more rows is the difference between seeing the whole of `calculate_shield_regeneration` and seeing most of it. Tightening the pitch shows strictly more, so this is a finding rather than a tension.

findings.location: Code pane header stack, y66–202
findings.finding: 136px — 16% of the pane — goes to four stacked header rows before the first line of code: the `CODE` title, the loop/iteration strip, the file tab row, and a two-line prose note. Three of those four are metadata about the listing rather than the listing. The note in particular restates in 110 characters what the line-number column already shows by starting at 26, and it costs two full code rows to do it. The header stack is the single largest block of non-content in the pane that has the most content to show.

findings.location: Code pane gutter — `·` on lines 26–50, `⊘` on line 29, `⊙` on line 32, blank on lines 30, 33, 36, 38, 39, 45, 47, 51
findings.finding: Three coverage states plus an ordinary executed dot are carried by marks roughly 4–7px wide in a 14px gutter. `ran` (a dot) versus `cannot tell` (nothing) is a four-pixel difference; `did not run` (`⊘`) versus `ran-branch-arm` (`⊙`) is a one-to-two-pixel interior difference. The information is genuinely there and the three states are genuinely distinct, which is a real gain over the previous round — but at this size the distinction is only available to a reader who already knows the legend, and there is no legend on the page. A slightly wider gutter would cost 6px and make the newest signal on the pane actually readable.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge — lines 26, 41, 42, 43, 48, 49
findings.finding: Six of twenty-six visible lines are cut at the pane border and the cut content is simply gone at this viewport, with no marker of how much is missing. Line 42's comment and line 49's expression are both cut mid-token. The right thing was dropped in the sense that the current position and the gutter survived, but a reader cannot tell a truncated line from a complete one, so the pane understates how much of the source it is actually withholding.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the row `Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded` directly above the DATA row
findings.finding: A raw enum identifier is printed as running text, with a prose label (`Status reason:`) in front of it and hyphen-joined lowercase tokens wrapping across two lines behind. Everywhere else this product converts machine state into product language — `Partial`, `Not observable`, `Synthetic demo data`, `By call order.` are all written, chosen phrases. Here the ViewModel's enum value leaks through unformatted, and it does so in the pane whose whole job in this register is to tell the reader what they are looking at and be trusted while doing it. The tone of copy is a design property in this product; this line is the one place on the surface where nobody wrote the copy.

findings.location: Code pane header (`line 4`), Transaction pane (`101:0`), Call Trace footer (`Self cost`)
findings.finding: Three in-pane navigation targets use the explorer register's link primitive — indigo, underlined, web-link styled. The sanctioned crossing between registers runs the other way (editor tokens into explorer pages); an underlined hyperlink inside a debugger pane is the explorer primitive crossing into the tool, and it does not read as deliberate: `Self cost` is a column toggle, `line 4` is a jump within the open file, and `101:0` is the only one of the three that leaves the session. Three different behaviours wearing one web-link costume. A desktop user would expect these to be pane affordances, not links.

findings.location: Transaction pane — the `Partial` badge in the pane header and the `Synthetic demo data` badge on the DATA row
findings.finding: Two badges of identical shape, size, border weight and corner radius sit 110px apart and belong to different semantic families: one is a transaction outcome, the other is a claim about the reality of every value on the page. Reusing one badge primitive across a status and a provenance marker is consistent, but it also means the page's most consequential statement is dressed exactly like a routine status chip — which is the fair reading of "is the row now too quiet". Provenance is the one thing here that should not share a costume with the ordinary.

findings.location: Page canvas behind and between the panes
findings.finding: The workspace behind the panes is pure black rather than the dark grey the CodeTracer desktop application uses, so the surface reads slightly toward a terminal or an OLED web dashboard rather than toward the desktop app it is meant to be continuous with. The panes themselves are correctly pitched; it is only the ground they sit on that reads as a web choice.

findings.location: Code pane, the note row "Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window."
findings.finding: The sentence is explanatory web copy in a tool pane, and it is doing a job the gutter already does by starting at 26. Its phrasing ("the lines above it are not in this window") also explains the widget's mechanics rather than stating a fact about the session. The desktop app states this kind of thing with a marker, not a sentence; if the sentence is needed, "Lines 1–25 are outside this window" says it without narrating the UI.

findings.location: Call Trace pane, column header `ACIR opcodes`
findings.finding: The header splits one column label across two emphasis levels — `ACIR` bright, `opcodes` dim — so it reads at a glance as two columns rather than one qualified one. Every other header on the page (`FRAME`, `CODE`, `VALUES`, `TRANSACTION`, `DATA`, `BLOCK`) is a single flat all-caps level, so this is the only place the header primitive varies.

findings.location: Code pane, line 42 comment — "shields regain a percentage of the maxium capacity after each h…"
findings.finding: A spelling error ("maxium" for "maximum") is visible in the fixture source on the register's flagship capture. It is fixture content rather than product copy, so it is not a design defect as such, but this image is the one a visitor sees first and the source listing is the product's showcase texture; a typo in it reads as carelessness about the demo.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `Data` row — the paragraph beneath the `Synthetic demo data` badge, above the `BLOCK` row
findings.finding: The page's most important claim is its worst-set text. The eight sentences are right-aligned in a ~250 px column, ragged on the left edge the eye returns to, while the two other paragraphs in the same pane (`EXECUTIONS`, `DECODED INPUT`) are set left — so the provenance block matches nothing else in the product and reads as prose that fell into the value column and took its alignment. It also consumes ~230 px, about 23% of the pane, which means the ~190 px the band gave back to the viewport was relocated and grown rather than reclaimed, and it pushes the pane's own fields down until `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)` is clipped at the viewport bottom. Set left at full pane width the same sentences run four to five lines and the fields come back above the fold; the wording needs no change.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `DATA` row, the provenance sentences beneath the `Synthetic demo data` badge
findings.finding: The eight-line provenance paragraph is right-aligned, so every line starts at a different x in a ~300px measure. It is the only right-aligned paragraph in the pane — the `aztec private function executed client-side…` note and the `This selector is not in any ABI…` note further down are both left-aligned and are visibly easier to read. Ragged-left is a poor setting for prose at any measure and a bad one at this width, and it is applied to the single passage this row exists to deliver.

findings.location: Transaction pane, every label from `DATA` down to `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)`
findings.finding: One uppercase, letterspaced, small style carries three different structural levels: section headings (`EXECUTIONS`, `DECODED INPUT`), row labels inside those sections (`SELECTOR`, `RAW`), and top-level row labels (`BLOCK`, `CANONICAL`, `FEE PAYER`). `DECODED INPUT` and the `SELECTOR` it contains are typographically identical, so the pane's nesting is only recoverable by reading the words and knowing the domain — hierarchy is not readable without reading.

findings.location: Transaction pane `COST · MANA` row versus Call Trace `ACIR opcodes` column
findings.finding: `88000 / 200000` is set without thousands separators while the call trace sets `1,315` and `1,208` with them, in the same viewport, both in mono. Two formatting conventions for five- and six-digit counts on one screen; the larger numbers are the ones left unseparated, so they are the harder pair to read at a glance.

findings.location: Code pane, the `Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below…` strip between the file tabs and line 26
findings.finding: UI copy is set in the monospace code face at the same size and near the same colour as the listing below it, so a sentence about the window reads as a line of the program. The pane's other UI text (`CODE`, the file tabs, `LOOP iterate_asteroids`) is differentiated; this string is not, and it sits directly above the code it describes where the confusion costs most.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `FEE PAYER` and `TARGET` rows
findings.finding: Both 40-hex addresses wrap onto a second, right-aligned line that breaks mid-byte (`…e2a272b5` / `e430d5d932`), producing a short ragged fragment with no ellipsis and no byte boundary. The identity bar and this pane's own first row truncate the same data type with a `…` instead, so the view uses two different strategies for hashes within 500px of each other.

findings.location: Transaction pane, first two rows
findings.finding: The truncated hash `0xb636167a…66d46359` is set larger and darker than the complete hash printed immediately beneath it, so the less informative form outranks the informative one and the pane opens by saying the same thing twice at two sizes.

findings.location: Code pane header strip, `Iteration 3 of 8`
findings.finding: `Iteration 3 of 8` is the largest and heaviest string anywhere in the Code pane — larger than the pane title `CODE`, than the active file tab `src/shield.nr`, and than the code itself. The loop coordinate is worth promoting, but at this weight it becomes the pane's headline and the file identity drops below the iteration chips.

findings.location: Call Trace pane, column header row, right-hand cell `ACIR opcodes`
findings.finding: The header cell mixes an all-caps letterspaced acronym with lowercase running text in one string, against the plain all-caps `FRAME` at the other end of the same row. The two ends of one header row read as two different type styles.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, lines 29 (`⊘`) and 32 (`⊙`)
findings.finding: The two branch-arm glyphs are drawn at roughly 9px, where the difference between them — an interior slash versus an interior dot — is about two pixels of detail. They read as one family and are clearly a pair with the plain `·` step dots, which is right, but at this size the ran/did-not-run distinction is carried mostly by colour and by the rail, not by the glyph. A one-step size increase for these two marks only would let the glyph carry its own meaning.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge of lines 40, 48 and 53
findings.finding: Long signatures fade out mid-identifier (`shield_regen_perce…`, `damage: Field, r…`) against a soft mask. The fade is an honest 'there is more' signal, but it is only ~30px wide and there is no scrollbar or count, so a reader cannot tell whether one parameter or five are hidden — and on line 40 what is hidden is the end of a function signature.

findings.location: middle column, Call Trace region between the `By call order.` footer (y≈325) and the region's bottom border (y≈672)
findings.finding: Roughly 345px of the tabbed region's ~605px height is blank — 57% of it — and it is bordered blank, so it reads as a pane with a hole rather than as breathing room. Directly below, the Values pane fits ten rows into 397px with only ~120px to spare, and the Transaction pane to the right is cut off mid-JSON by the viewport bottom. Two of the three panes are short and the one with slack is the one holding it. The measurement the change did not make: the Values pane, not the tab region, is the one that should have the height at this viewport.

findings.location: Transaction pane, horizontal rules between rows
findings.finding: Three rule treatments in one pane. The first four rows (`Partial`+hash, full hash, `Status reason`, `DATA`+prose) have no separators at all. `BLOCK` through `COST · MANA` are separated by hairlines that run full-bleed into the pane border on both sides. `SELECTOR` and `RAW` are separated by hairlines inset about 10px from each edge. The pane consequently reads as three stacked tables that happen to share a border, and the inset rules make `DECODED INPUT` look like a different component rather than a section of the same list.

findings.location: Transaction pane, badge positions across the `Partial`, `DATA`, `CANONICAL`/`FINALITY` and `EXECUTIONS` rows
findings.finding: One badge component is placed four different ways in the same 1000px column: `Partial` flush left at the label edge; `Synthetic demo data` flush right at the value edge; `Yes` and `Safe` flush right; `Not observable` and `Trace ready` inline immediately after the words `private` and `public`, left-of-centre. There is no rule a reader can infer for where a badge will be, so the pane has no scannable badge column in either direction.

findings.location: identity bar, from the divider after `block 101` (x≈345) to the phase rail (x≈1478)
findings.finding: The gaps between the four stepping-control groups measure 16–25px; the gap between the scrubber and `Engine loading — 18 MB` measures ~15px, and between `1315` and the phase rail ~17px. One spacing value therefore separates things that belong together (two halves of the stepping cluster) and things that do not (a control from a status readout). Only the identity block is set apart, by a divider and by tighter 5–9px internal gaps. From the divider rightwards the bar reads as an even run of nine objects rather than as three or four groups.

findings.location: Code pane, the overflow chips below lines 26 and 48
findings.finding: The `+3` and `+2` chips are pushed onto a half-row of their own beneath their line and right-aligned to the pane edge, so the listing's steady ~23px row pitch jumps to ~46px twice and the eye loses the line grid at exactly the two places it is asked to count. Worse, the `+2` belonging to line 48 lands about 25px above line 49's own `+2`: two identical chips stacked at the right margin, the upper one vertically nearer the line it does not belong to.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `SELECTOR` and `RAW` rows
findings.finding: The `0x` values sit roughly 3px below their labels' baseline in both rows, where `BLOCK`, `CANONICAL`, `FINALITY` and `COST · MANA` all baseline-align label and value. The offset is small but it is the only place in the pane where the two columns of a row do not sit on one line.

findings.location: column widths — Code ~912px, middle ~605px, Transaction ~385px
findings.finding: The Transaction pane is narrow enough that both 40-hex addresses (`FEE PAYER`, `TARGET`) wrap to a second line, and the JSON block clips horizontally. Meanwhile the middle column is holding 345px of unused vertical space. The split was chosen without reference to the longest atomic value the narrowest pane must hold; ~60px taken from the middle column would put each address on one line.

findings.location: Code pane, bottom border at y≈1073, line 61
findings.finding: The listing is cut horizontally through the middle of line 61's glyphs by the pane border, with no fade and no partial-row mask — while the same pane's right-edge overflow on lines 40, 48 and 53 does get a soft fade. Two overflow treatments on the two axes of one pane.

findings.location: Code pane, inline value chips on lines 27, 28, 32, 49 and 50
findings.finding: Chips are placed wherever their code line happens to end — x≈322 on line 27, x≈345 on line 28, x≈490 on line 32, x≈740 on line 49, x≈290 on line 50 — forming a ragged second column, while the `+N` chips from the same family are right-aligned to the pane edge. Two alignment rules for one component within eight lines of each other.

findings.location: Values pane, `masses` row
findings.finding: The array `[100, 2000, 200, 100, 100, 50, 50, 14]` is right-aligned like every other value, so its left end reaches x≈1129 — about 150px from the `masses` label, where every other row leaves 250px or more. The value column therefore has no left boundary, and the one row that could use a gutter is the one that has none.

findings.location: Transaction pane `DATA` row badge (`Synthetic demo data`) and identity bar phase rail (`FETCHING`)
findings.finding: Both use the identical token pair — #dbeafe fill with #1e40af text and border. One colour role therefore means two unrelated things on one screen: 'the data you are looking at is not real' and 'the engine is currently in this phase'. Because the active phase pill is the only other saturated blue in view, the provenance badge inherits its in-progress reading, and the outlined-pill shape makes it look pressable besides. Provenance needs a tone that no transient state uses.

findings.location: Code pane gutter at lines 29–32, and the identity bar scrubber
findings.finding: Four cyans carry four meanings: #a5f3fc is the current-line band (and the selected call-trace row), #164e63 the current-position rail at x5-6, #0e7490 the new ran-arm rail at x7-8 and the `⊙` glyph, #155e75 the scrubber's filled portion; the plain `·` step dots are cyan too. On line 32 three of those shades stack inside eight horizontal pixels, so the mark that means 'this arm ran' is the same hue as the mark that means 'you are here' and is drawn immediately beside it on the band that also means 'you are here'. The one line where the new state appears is the one line where it cannot be read separately from position.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, `⊘` at line 29 versus `⊙` at line 32
findings.finding: The two members of the new pair are not one family in contrast or in role colour. `⊘` is #484848 on white at 9.15:1; `⊙` is #0e7490 on the #a5f3fc band at 4.29:1 — the weakest text-or-mark pair on the page, and more than a factor of two apart from its own counterpart. Worse, the emphasis is inverted: the accent goes to 'this ran', which is the unsurprising fact, while 'this did not run' — the fact worth finding — is drawn in #484848, the same grey as `Engine loading — 18 MB`, the `CODE` pane title and the provenance prose, so the skipped-branch state carries no status colour at all.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `DATA` row (label, badge and the sentences beneath)
findings.finding: The row has no surface tint, no border and no rule of its own. Its label is #565656, byte-identical to `BLOCK`, `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)` and the bar's `NOIR`; its sentences are #484848, byte-identical to the `aztec private function executed client-side…` footnote further down the same pane. Colour therefore gives the provenance claim exactly the weight of a routine footnote, and its only chromatic elevation is a badge that shares its tokens with a loading phase. Having removed a ~190px band, the row has swung to zero elevation — a light tint behind the row, or a provenance-only accent, would restore the claim without restoring the interruption.

findings.location: Values pane `remaining_shield` and `damage` rows, Code pane `damage: 0→2000` chip, and the `Partial` badge in both the identity bar and the Transaction pane
findings.finding: Amber carries two meanings. As diff it is excellent and consistent across panes — #854d0e text with an amber left rail in Values, an amber-bordered chip on line 32 — so 'changed at this step' reads the same everywhere. But `Partial` uses #ffedd5/#9a3412 from the same family as a transaction status, and the two uses sit about 300px apart with the Values pane's oranges directly below the badge. The shades differ enough to be told apart on inspection, not at a glance.

findings.location: surface tokens across the page — inter-pane gaps, Transaction pane JSON block, pane headers, Code pane value chips
findings.finding: #ececeb is both the page background showing through the 4px inter-pane gaps and the fill of the recessed JSON block inside the Transaction pane, so an inset surface is the same colour as 'outside all panes'. #f3f3f3 (the `Not observable` badge fill) sits seven units from #ececeb and is a functional duplicate rung. #dddddd serves as both every pane header fill and every inline value chip in the Code pane. The ladder works, but it has one rung too many and two rungs doing two jobs each.

findings.location: Call Trace pane footer (`Self cost`) and Transaction pane `BLOCK` row (`101:0`)
findings.finding: Both are #4f46e5 indigo with an underline — document-link chrome, and a fifth blue-family hue alongside #1e40af and the three cyans. In a tool pane an underlined indigo string reads as a navigation link rather than as the control `Self cost` appears to be, and it adds a hue that carries no role elsewhere in the register.

findings.location: Code pane, right-edge overflow fade on lines 40, 48 and 53
findings.finding: The fade bottoms out at about #ababab on white — 2.3:1 — partway through an identifier. As a mask that is the intent and it is legible where it matters, but on line 40 what dissolves is the tail of a function signature, and the gradient gives no cue how much is hidden. A fade that resolves at a token boundary, or a count, would not ask the reader to judge whether the grey characters are still text.

findings.location: whole page palette
findings.finding: Every colour resolves to a default utility-framework ramp step — blue-100/800, green-100/800, orange-100/800, cyan-200/700/900, indigo-600 and the neutral greys. The result is cohesive, but the cohesion belongs to the ramp rather than to this product, which is also why two unrelated roles landed on exactly #dbeafe/#1e40af. Nothing in the surface colour says CodeTracer specifically the way the syntax palette does.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `Data` row — prose block beneath the `Synthetic demo data` badge
findings.finding: The provenance sentences are set right-aligned in a ~250 px column, so eight lines run ragged on the left edge the eye returns to; the block costs ~230 px, roughly 23% of the pane, and pushes the chain fields down until `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)` is clipped at the viewport bottom. Set left-aligned and full pane width it is four or five lines and the fields come back above the fold.

findings.location: Call Trace region, below the `By call order.` footer; and Values pane below the `i` row
findings.finding: Measured: the tabbed region runs y≈70–662 and its last frame ends at y≈301, leaving 332 px — 56% of the region — blank; Values runs y≈675–1080 with its last row at y≈951, leaving a further 129 px. 461 px, 46% of the middle column, is empty at a seven-frame fixture while the Transaction pane beside it is clipped. Neither pane should hold that height by fixed share: size the tab region to its frames and let Values take the remainder.

findings.location: Code pane, listing area (lines 26–61)
findings.finding: Line pitch measures ~23 px against ~13 px monospace glyphs — a line-height near 1.75, marketing leading in the register's densest pane. The pane just gained the band's ~190 px and spent it on air: at desktop-app leading the same area carries roughly nine more source lines, which is the difference between seeing the whole `calculate_damage` body and scrolling for it.

findings.location: Code pane gutter, lines 26–34 (`⊙` on 32, `⊘` on 29, `·` elsewhere)
findings.finding: The three coverage states read as one family and are unambiguous when magnified, but at 1:1 the glyphs occupy about seven pixels and `⊙` and `⊘` reduce to near-identical dark blobs — a centre dot versus a diagonal stroke is the whole distinction, and the 3 px rail beside them is the only cue that survives at a glance. The one state that is legible from across the pane, the teal `·`, is the least informative of the three.

findings.location: Identity bar — the four stepping button pairs and the scrubber between them and `Engine loading`
findings.finding: Eight icon buttons carry no labels and no key hints, so the densest control cluster on the page is the only one that tells the reader nothing about itself; beside them the ~255 px scrubber is the widest element in the bar and encodes exactly the one number `128 / 1315` already states in text, with no frame or event structure along its length.

findings.location: Transaction pane, right column — the whole label/value stack from `Data` through `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)`
findings.finding: This pane is the explorer's transaction overview transplanted whole: ~30 px label/value rows separated by hairline rules, labels in the proportional face, three multi-line paragraphs in sentence-case body type, and pill values (`Yes`, `Safe`) where the tool register would print the word. Beside Call Trace and Values — which are genuinely desktop-app tables — the third pane reads as a web page docked to a debugger rather than a pane of it, and the register boundary the product treats as deliberate is invisible inside this column.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `Data` row — the eight-line paragraph under the `Synthetic demo data` badge
findings.finding: The row is not too quiet for the claim — it is too explorer for this register. It is set as a right-aligned paragraph in the proportional face, while the two lesser paragraphs in the same pane (`EXECUTIONS`, `DECODED INPUT`) are set left; the provenance claim is therefore the one block in the product whose text alignment matches nothing else, which reads as the band's marketing setting inherited into a value column rather than a decision. The sentences themselves are exactly right and should not be shortened.

findings.location: Code pane, the strip above line 26: "Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below…"
findings.finding: A full-width sentence of explanatory prose at the top of the densest pane. The tone is right and the fact is worth stating, but this is the instinct the register just removed one level up when the provenance band came out — the desktop app marks a window boundary with a fold or an ellipsis row in the gutter, not with a sentence spanning the pane.

findings.location: Code pane header — iteration chip `3`, file tab `src/shield.nr`, and the `CALL TRACE` tab
findings.finding: One gesture, three drawings, all within 200 px of each other: the file tab is selected by a single near-black underline, the `CALL TRACE` tab by the same rule in a different weight, and iteration `3` by a teal numeral over a teal rule with a second black rule beneath it inside a filled chip. Only one of the three uses the accent, and only one carries two rules; a shared primitive should be recognisable as itself across the pane.

findings.location: Identity bar, right end — the `NOIR` label beside the share and download buttons
findings.finding: Every other state token on the page wears the badge shape — `Partial`, `Synthetic demo data`, `Not observable`, `Trace ready`, `Yes`, `Safe` — but the one naming the language of everything in the Code pane is bare uppercase text, so it reads as a wordmark fragment rather than as a member of the badge family.

findings.location: Transaction pane (right rail, x≈1531-1911), the `DATA` row's sentence block at y≈205-525, set in the value column beneath the `Real Aztec testnet data` badge
findings.finding: The band was the right thing to remove and this row is the right place to put provenance. What was built is a paragraph dropped into a value cell, and it is now the weakest element on the page — weaker than the raw hex fee, because the fee costs a reader one fact while this costs them the page's entire claim. Three things are wrong with it and they compound. (a) Alignment: fifteen lines of body prose set flush-right and ragged-left. Every line begins at a different x, so the return sweep has no anchor and the block must be read rather than scanned. Nothing else on the page is set this way, and this is the one block a reader must actually read. (b) Measure: roughly 28 characters, because the value column of a 369px pane is what the row inherited. It breaks `aztec-` / `testnet.drpc.org` and `2026-` / `08-31T07:40:55.566Z` across lines — the endpoint and the moment, the two facts that make the provenance checkable, are the two the wrapping mangles — and it hides the paragraph break, so `are published here.` and `Transactions below block` sit on adjacent lines with nothing between them. (c) Cost: ~320px, the tallest block in the pane, spent in the one region on the page whose content already exceeds its box. The Transaction pane clips at the viewport bottom mid `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)` object, and what is no longer on screen is the replay telemetry — instructions executed, effects matched, `effectsMismatched: 0` — the evidence that this replay reproduced the chain's own effects. The band cost 190px of everyone's height; this row costs 320px of the only pane that had something to lose, so the trade returned space to three panes that had nothing to put in it and took it from the one that did. The pane itself proves the fix: the selector explanation at y≈855-910 is the same kind of prose, set left-aligned across the pane's full width, and it reads cleanly in three lines. Set the provenance sentences the same way, full pane width under the label and badge, and the row becomes about a third of its current height and legible at a glance.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row — the provenance sentences beginning "Captured from aztec-testnet.drpc.org"
findings.finding: Eleven lines of running prose are set right-aligned, inheriting the value column's alignment from the label/value rows above. Ragged-left prose gives the eye no fixed return edge, and the measure is roughly 28 characters, so the sentence that carries the page's central claim breaks mid-phrase eleven times ("(50" / "blocks) at that moment. 6" / "transaction(s) inside it were"). This is the one paragraph in the pane a reader is meant to read end to end and it is the least readable text on the page.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row label and badge, vs the BLOCK / CANONICAL / FINALITY rows beneath it
findings.finding: The provenance row has no typographic promotion. Its label is the same ~10px tracked uppercase grey as CANONICAL and FINALITY, its badge is the same small pill as `Yes` and `Pending`, and it sits fourth in a run of ten visually identical rows. Graded as content rather than decoration, the type ranks it as one metadata row among ten — a reader scanning the pane without reading will not learn that this is the row telling them the data is real.

findings.location: Transaction pane, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row
findings.finding: The 32-byte fee prints as 64 hex characters in full, wrapping across three right-aligned monospace lines that are almost entirely zeros, with the unit `mana (FeeJuice)` orphaned on a fourth line at a smaller grey size. No truncation is applied at a meaningful boundary and no digit grouping separates the leading zero run from the significant tail `185cfcc84d2f103f`, even though the identity bar 40px above demonstrates the product's own truncation idiom (`0x0858d6…7fb2`). Four lines of type are spent on one number whose informative part is sixteen characters.

findings.location: Transaction pane — `DECODED INPUT` and `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)` against the row labels `SELECTOR`, `RAW`, `BLOCK`, `EXECUTIONS`
findings.finding: Section headers and row labels share one treatment (same size, weight, tracking, case and colour), so DECODED INPUT reads as a row whose value is missing rather than as a heading owning SELECTOR and RAW beneath it. The pane's ten rows are therefore one flat list at one level, when the content is two levels deep. EXECUTIONS has the same ambiguity — it looks like a label whose value is the `public` line below rather than beside it.

findings.location: Transaction pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block at the pane's foot
findings.finding: The replay telemetry — the instruction count and the matched/mismatched effect counts that are the evidence this session reproduced the chain — is rendered only as more keys inside the raw JSON payload, typeset identically to `l2BlockNumber` and `revertCode` and beginning below the viewport edge. The load-bearing claim of the whole view gets no type-level status: it is the same 12px mono at the same weight as the payload's bookkeeping fields.

findings.location: Code pane body copy vs Transaction pane body copy (the DATA sentences and "This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds…")

findings.location: Transaction pane, full hash line beneath the `Succeeded` badge

findings.location: the three-column split — Code (x≈8–917), Call Trace/Values (x≈921–1527), Transaction (x≈1531–1912)

findings.location: Transaction pane, DATA row (y≈178–530)

findings.location: Call Trace pane (y≈95–668) and Values pane (y≈700–1072), below their explanatory lines

findings.location: Code pane — header `CODE` (x≈16), body paragraphs (x≈22), `Supply sources` button border box (x≈14)

findings.location: identity bar, the stepping control cluster (x≈470–760)

findings.location: identity bar — progress bar (x≈775–1035) and phase rail (x≈1320–1570)

findings.location: Transaction pane — `Real Aztec testnet data` badge (DATA row), `Succeeded` badge (hash row) and `Trace ready` badge (EXECUTIONS row); plus `Succeeded` in the identity bar

findings.location: surface levels across the whole page — canvas behind the panes, pane bodies, and the CODE / CALL TRACE / TRANSACTION / VALUES header strips

A designed light theme for this register would give the pane body one step of separation from the canvas and the header strip a second, as the desktop app's surfaces do.

findings.location: Transaction pane row labels (DATA, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE, EXECUTIONS, SELECTOR, RAW) and the `mana (FeeJuice)` unit line

findings.location: identity bar — progress bar fill (x≈775–865), active phase chip `FETCHING` (x≈1320–1400), and the link colours on `aztec-testnet` and `63675:0`

The first two express the same concept — how far the engine has loaded — in different hues 450px apart, and neither matches the accent used for navigation. Whether these are three roles or one hue family drifting is not readable from the page.

findings.location: Transaction pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block (y≈945 to the viewport edge)
findings.finding: This is the only tinted surface in the pane — a pale grey-blue panel — yet its content is rendered in a single near-black with no token colour: keys, numbers and booleans (`63675`, `0`, `true`) are indistinguishable by hue. In the register whose reference is the CodeTracer editor, a chain-native payload is the one place a reader scans for a value's type, and the palette that exists for exactly that is not applied.

findings.location: Code pane below `Supply sources`, and Call Trace / Values panes below their explanatory lines
findings.finding: The empty regions are the same flat white as the populated ones, so nothing tonal marks them as deliberately empty. With `Engine loading — 18 MB` and an active `FETCHING` phase in the bar directly above, a plain white void is exactly what a not-yet-painted pane would look like, and the visual treatment therefore undercuts sentences that say the emptiness is the chain's limitation and final. A faint recessed tone for the region — the desktop app's treatment for an inert pane — would make the emptiness read as an answer.

findings.location: Transaction pane — `Yes` (CANONICAL) and `Pending` (FINALITY) badges
findings.finding: Both render as the same neutral grey pill, so an established affirmative fact and a state that has not yet resolved share one tone while a resolved outcome two rows above gets green. Neutral for `Pending` is right; neutral for `Yes` leaves the badge family with no legible rule about when tone is applied.

findings.location: the four-pane split: Code pane (left, x≈8-917), Call Trace and Values (centre, x≈922-1527) against the Transaction pane (right rail, x≈1531-1911, clipping at the viewport bottom mid `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)` JSON)
findings.finding: One pane is starved while three sit empty. The Code pane is ~910px wide and ~1010px tall and holds four lines of prose and one button in its top 240px; ~770px below `Supply sources` is blank. Call Trace holds two lines in a 600x580 region, Values two lines in a 600x390 region. The Transaction pane is the only region on the page whose content exceeds its box, and it is the narrowest: at 369px the provenance sentences wrap to fifteen lines, the fee wraps to three, the raw JSON wraps at four tokens a line, and the pane is cut off mid-object at y=1080. What falls off is the replay telemetry — instructions executed, effects matched and `effectsMismatched: 0`, the evidence that this replay reproduced the chain's own effects, which is the whole claim of the view. The 1080px viewport has ~1550px of horizontal space carrying six sentences and ~370px carrying everything else. Removing the provenance band returned ~190px of height to every pane; the new `DATA` row then consumed ~320px inside the Transaction pane, so the one pane that could use height is net worse off while the three panes with nothing to show got taller. A wider right rail at this viewport, or the provenance prose set across the pane's full width instead of in the value column, would put the telemetry back on screen without dropping anything.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the `DATA` row's sentence block, y≈205-525, set in the value column beneath the `Real Aztec testnet data` badge
findings.finding: The provenance sentences are right-aligned and ragged-left over fifteen lines at roughly a 28-character measure, inside the value column of a label/value grid. Right-aligned body prose is the least scannable text configuration available: every line starts at a different x, so the return sweep has no anchor, and at 28 characters the block breaks mid-token (`aztec-` / `testnet.drpc.org`, `2026-` / `08-31T07:40:55.566Z`) and hides its paragraph break — the sentence ending `are published here.` and the one beginning `Transactions below block` sit on adjacent lines with nothing to separate them. The same pane proves the better treatment exists: the selector explanation at y≈855-910 is left-aligned across the pane's full width and reads in three lines. This row is carrying the page's most important claim and is the hardest text on the page to read.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `COST · TRANSACTIONFEE` row between FINALITY and EXECUTIONS, y≈632-710
findings.finding: The fee is a 32-byte word printed raw: `0x` followed by 64 nibbles wrapping across three right-aligned lines, of which roughly 46 are literal zero padding and only `185cfcc84d2f103f` carries information, stranded at the end of the third line. A reader cannot read the quantity, compare it to another fee, or sanity-check its magnitude. The row also stands about four times the height of BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY above it, so the pane's densest vertical space is spent on padding zeroes. The label is the adapter's camelCase field uppercased into the unbroken token `TRANSACTIONFEE`, sitting beside BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY and DECODED INPUT, all of which are English. Decode to a decimal figure with the raw word available on demand.

findings.location: Code pane, the ~770px below the `Supply sources` button (y≈320-1075), and the Call Trace pane below its single paragraph
findings.finding: The page states that stepping is complete at instruction level and the identity bar proves it — the position readout reads `128 / 345`, so 345 program counters and a frame stack exist in this recording. None of it is surfaced anywhere. The panes are empty by necessity of the missing source text, not of the missing trace, and a program-counter column or an unnamed frame list would fill the emptiest regions on the page with real recorded content rather than argument for it. This is a refinement rather than a defect: what is shown is honest and each pane explains itself, and the fix adds information rather than removing it.

findings.location: the three source-starved pane interiors: Code pane paragraph at y≈120-250, Call Trace paragraph at y≈115-155, Values paragraph at y≈715-755
findings.finding: The explanations are correct content in the wrong register. Each is set as flowing body prose at roughly a 590px measure, flush to the top-left of an otherwise empty pane, with no framing of any kind — no muted block, no rule, no centring, no icon, nothing that says `this pane has a state`. That is the explorer register's treatment of a paragraph, and the panes it sits in are 910x1010 and 600x580. A CodeTracer desktop user reads a pane whose entire content is a left-aligned essay as an unstyled or failed render, not as a designed empty state; the desktop idiom for `this pane cannot fill` is compact, muted and visibly a status, not a document. The shell around it is right — slim identity bar, uppercase pane headers, grouped stepping controls, underline tabs on CALL TRACE / EVENT LOG — which makes the crossing inside the panes read as unintentional rather than deliberate. The fix is presentation, not content: keep every sentence, give it the tool's empty-state treatment.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the `COST · TRANSACTIONFEE` label in the label column, between FINALITY and EXECUTIONS at y≈640
findings.finding: The label is the adapter's camelCase field name uppercased into the unbroken token `TRANSACTIONFEE`, sitting in a column whose other entries — BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, EXECUTIONS, DECODED INPUT, SELECTOR — are all product English. Copy is a design property in this product and this is a vocabulary leak from the data layer onto the surface. It is more pointed here than it would be elsewhere, because the same pane already has a sanctioned home for chain-native identifiers: the `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)` block at the pane's foot, where `l2BlockNumber`, `txIndexInBlock` and `bodyRetainedAtCapture` are camelCase precisely because they are the chain's own field names and are labelled as such. `TRANSACTIONFEE` has escaped that block into the label column, so the one boundary the pane draws between product vocabulary and adapter vocabulary is broken by a single row.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the provenance row's label `DATA` at y≈185
findings.finding: With `debugLayout` dropping the nav and the footer, this row is now the only place on the page that answers whose data the reader is looking at, and its label is the most generic word in the pane. `BLOCK`, `CANONICAL`, `FINALITY` and `SELECTOR` each name the question their value answers; `DATA` does not — the badge beside it carries the whole burden of saying that this is a real testnet capture. The row is not too quiet in size or tone — it is first in the pane, the badge is affirmative and matches `Succeeded` and `Trace ready`, and the capture's own sentences follow it — but a label such as `SOURCE` or `PROVENANCE` would make it findable by a reader scanning the label column for the question rather than noticing the badge.

findings.location: Code pane, the standalone line `Stepping continues at instruction level.` at y≈240, one paragraph gap below the main explanation
findings.finding: The main paragraph already ends `Stepping is complete; only the text is missing.` The standalone line restates it in weaker words a paragraph later, so the pane's last word on the subject is its least specific one. Separated by a full paragraph gap and set at the same size and weight as the paragraph above, it reads as a second thought appended to a finished statement rather than as a designed two-part message. Either make it a distinct register — a quiet status line under the explanation, tied to the `Supply sources` affordance below it — or drop it, since the sentence it repeats is stronger.

findings.location: Decoded input section — the bordered note card directly beneath the SELECTOR / RAW two-row grid
findings.finding: The note asserts a state that is not the one rendered 40px above it. `SELECTOR` is an em dash and `RAW` is `0x`, yet the note says the selector is unknown to BlockTracer's ABIs, that the parameters are therefore shown as raw bytes, and that supplying an ABI would decode them. No selector exists, no parameters are shown, no bytes are present, and no ABI can decode a body the chain no longer serves — the page's own Raw (chain-native) block states `"bodyRetainedAtCapture": false`. This is the pruned-body absence, presented as a missing-ABI absence, with an offered remedy that cannot succeed; `RAW 0x` compounds it by rendering unavailable calldata as empty calldata. On a page whose entire purpose is to distinguish 'permanently unknowable' from 'not fetched yet' — and which does that correctly in the Not observable card, Events, Internal calls and State changes — this is the one paragraph that misinforms, and it is the weakest thing on the page for exactly that reason.

findings.location: Decoded input section — the SELECTOR/RAW grid and the note card directly beneath it
findings.finding: The note reads "This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds, so the parameters are shown as raw bytes", but SELECTOR renders the em-dash no-value glyph and RAW renders a bare `0x`. There is no selector and there are no bytes, so the sentence describes a different state than the one typeset above it. The two rows also use two different glyphs for the same absence — `—` in one and an empty `0x` in the next — so a reader cannot tell whether the em-dash means unknown and `0x` means empty, or the reverse.

findings.location: Overview grid, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row, value cell
findings.finding: A cost is set as a 66-character zero-padded hex word (`0x0000…0175c1a29c1f97278 mana (FeeJuice)`), the longest unbroken token on the page, running nearly the full width of the value column. Sixty leading zeros carry no information yet occupy most of the line, the significant digits are buried at the far right, and there is no tabular decimal figure, no digit grouping and no truncation at a meaningful boundary with the full value obtainable. Every other numeric on the page (block 67113, the 67120–67144 range) is set as a readable number; this one is not.

findings.location: Overview grid, label column, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row
findings.finding: The uppercase letterspaced label style is applied to a raw camelCase source identifier, producing `TRANSACTIONFEE` — a fourteen-character run with the word boundary destroyed, next to labels that are real words (DATA, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY). It is also the only label in the column that wraps to two lines, and it wraps after the middot, leaving `COST ·` hanging at the end of line one.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row, third line of the capture paragraph
findings.finding: "NO TRANSACTION INSIDE IT WAS REPLAYABLE" is set in full capitals inside running body prose. Capitals are the crudest emphasis device available and here they collide with an established meaning: every other capitalised run on this page is a field label or the eyebrow, so the reader has already learned that caps signals "label", not "emphasis". The effect is a shout in the middle of the one paragraph whose job is to sound calm and factual.

findings.location: Overview grid — DATA row against the BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY rows
findings.finding: The provenance row does land first, before the empty sections, which is what the revision needed. But its nine lines of prose are set at exactly the size, weight and colour of the single-line values below it, so nothing typographic separates the claim (the `Real Aztec mainnet data` badge) from the capture narrative that supports it, and nothing separates either from the ordinary metadata. The grid therefore opens with a block roughly seven times the height of any other row at the same level, and block, canonicality and finality read as a footnote to it. One extra level — a lead sentence at a heavier weight, or the narrative at a step down — would let the row assert its claim without swamping the facts.

findings.location: Page eyebrow "TRANSACTION" above the H1, versus the Overview grid label column
findings.finding: The page's top-level kicker and the field labels three levels down share size, case, letterspacing, weight and colour. They are distinguishable only by position and by the rule that precedes the eyebrow, so the type scale spends one level twice instead of marking the difference between "what this page is" and "what this cell holds".

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) block
findings.finding: Keys and values in the JSON are typographically identical — same monospace face, same weight, same colour — so the shape of the object has to be read rather than seen. A weight or emphasis split between key and value would make the five fields scannable at a glance, which is the only reason this block is on the page.

findings.location: Content column — the Not observable card, Decoded-input note and the three empty-section notes, versus the Overview grid, the Decoded-input grid and the Raw (chain-native) block
findings.finding: The column has two right edges. The Overview grid, the Decoded input grid and the Raw block all terminate at the content column's right edge (the same edge as the nav's resolver field and the footer disclosure); every note and notice card stops roughly 210px short of it. Both edges recur several times, so neither reads as an exception — the page simply has two right margins stacked down its length, and the ragged right side is the first thing the eye catches when scanning the page vertically. The worst instance is at the top: the `Not observable` card, which carries the single most important message on the page, is narrower than the metadata grid immediately below it, so the layout ranks the table above the explanation.

findings.location: Section separators between Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes and Raw (chain-native)
findings.finding: Six headings at one level get two different separation treatments. Overview, Decoded input, Events and Raw (chain-native) are each preceded by a full-width hairline rule and a large gap; Internal calls and State changes are preceded by no rule and roughly half the gap. Because proximity is the only grouping cue available at this level, the layout asserts that Events, Internal calls and State changes form one group — but the content splits the other way: Events is sourced from the receipt, Internal calls and State changes from the trace that does not exist. Either give all six the same rule and gap, or make the grouping real by demoting the grouped headings a level and letting the rule mean something.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row, label cell
findings.finding: The DATA row is about seven times the height of any other row in the grid, and its label cell holds one short word at the top with roughly 220px of empty tinted column beneath it. The void is the largest single area of unused surface inside any container on the page, and it sits immediately left of the densest paragraph. Either let the label cell shrink-wrap its label with the value cell spanning, or give the row a different internal layout from the four single-line rows it shares a grid with.

findings.location: Not observable card (top of page) versus the Decoded-input, Events, Internal calls and State changes note cards
findings.finding: The same card primitive appears in two elevations: the Not observable card sits on a soft drop shadow, the other four are flat with a hairline edge. If the shadow is meant to mark primacy it is the only such marker on the page and nothing else repeats it; if it is not, it is an inconsistent edge treatment on a component used five times.

findings.location: Whole page at the 1920px viewport
findings.finding: The page is a single centred ribbon of roughly 910px with about 500px of empty canvas on each side, and no element at any point uses the extra width. Below the Overview grid the used area drops to about 700px, so at this viewport more than two thirds of the screen is canvas while the DATA row's paragraph wraps to nine lines. Centring the column is the right instinct for the register, but the widest viewport should buy something — pairing the provenance narrative beside the four one-line facts, for example, rather than stacking them.

findings.location: Footer, right-hand column — the provenance sentence and the Source on GitHub link beneath it
findings.finding: The two lines of the footer's right column agree on neither edge. The provenance sentence is set flush to the column's right edge; the Source on GitHub line below it starts a few pixels left of that sentence's left edge — close enough to read as a misalignment rather than a decision — and ends far short of the right edge. The left column directly opposite holds a clean shared left edge for both its lines, which makes the right column's near-miss more conspicuous.

findings.location: The Succeeded badge beside the H1, the FINALITY row's Finalized badge, and the DATA row's Real Aztec mainnet data badge — all in the Overview grid or directly above it
findings.finding: One green, three meanings, all visible at once: execution outcome, consensus phase, and the provenance of the data itself. The first two are statuses of the transaction; the third is a claim about where the bytes came from and is not a status at all, yet it is the affirmative green that the page has just taught the reader means "this succeeded". The result is that the Overview grid opens with what scans as a third approval chip rather than as a source attribution. The expectation asks for an affirmative tone here and that is right — but affirmative does not have to be the same swatch as the outcome badge. A distinct treatment (different hue in the accent family, or a filled versus outlined split) would keep the tone affirmative while letting each colour mean one thing.

findings.location: Not observable badge in the notice card, versus the Yes chip in the Overview grid's CANONICAL row
findings.finding: The two are tonally identical — dark text, near-white fill, hairline neutral border, the badge's leading dot the only difference. Neutral is the correct family here (an error or warning tone would be the P1 this page exists to avoid), but neutrality has been applied at the same strength to the single fact that distinguishes this transaction from every other one on the site and to a routine boolean. Against three saturated green chips, the page's most consequential state is also its quietest coloured element, so a reader scanning by colour alone takes away "succeeded, canonical, finalized, real data" and never reaches the reason. A stronger neutral — a filled surface, a darker border, or a distinct emphasis tone — would carry the weight without implying failure.

findings.location: Breadcrumb (Home, aztec-mainnet) and the Overview grid's BLOCK link, versus the footer link rows (About, Chains, Privacy & settings) and the provenance strip links (Metacraft Labs, CodeTracer, Source on GitHub)
findings.finding: Links appear in two colours on one page: an accent blue in the breadcrumb and in the BLOCK cell, near-black in the footer's two link rows and the provenance strip. All are underlined, so the underline rather than the colour is the only reliable signal a reader can learn. The de-emphasis reads as deliberate for footer chrome, but it means the accent hue does not have a single role: it is a link colour above the fold and a brand colour below it.

findings.location: Overview and Decoded-input grids, label column (DATA, BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE, SELECTOR, RAW) and the page eyebrow TRANSACTION
findings.finding: This is the page's lowest-contrast text-on-surface pair: mid-grey uppercase set very small on the tinted label column. It is legible here, but it sits closer to the floor than anything else on the page while also being the smallest type, which is the combination the floor exists to prevent. The green badge text on its pale green fill is the next lowest pair. Both would benefit from a step of darkening rather than being left at the threshold.

findings.location: Overview and Decoded-input grids — the tinted label column against the page canvas
findings.finding: The label column's tint and the page canvas sit at almost the same value, so the grid's left column visually continues into the canvas and only the container's hairline border keeps the grid contained. The surface ladder is otherwise clear (canvas, white card, tinted cell); pushing the label tint one step away from the canvas value — or the canvas one step away from it — would make the grid read as a discrete object rather than as a white column floating on a grey field.

findings.location: Footer provenance strip — the heart in "Built with" and the CodeTracer mark
findings.finding: Both marks are properly drawn vector glyphs, clearly visible against the footer surface, with no tofu, no emoji-presentation fallback and no invisibility — the P1 conditions do not apply. They are, however, rendered in the brand blue rather than taking their colour from the near-black sentence they sit inside, while the GitHub mark on the line below does inherit the text colour. Within one four-line strip the same class of inline mark is therefore coloured two different ways.

findings.location: Decoded input section — the note card directly below the SELECTOR / RAW grid
findings.finding: The note reads "This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds, so the parameters are shown as raw bytes. Supplying an ABI decodes them." Directly above it, SELECTOR is an em dash and RAW is `0x`: there is no selector, there are no parameters, and no raw bytes are shown. The Raw (chain-native) block at the foot of the page states `"bodyRetainedAtCapture": false` — the input is unavailable because the body was pruned, which is the same fact the page explains carefully twice elsewhere. Here that absence is instead attributed to BlockTracer's ABI holdings and closed with a remedy that cannot succeed. Three of the page's four content sections state the correct permanent reason; this one states a wrong, transient-sounding one, and `RAW 0x` presents unavailable calldata as empty calldata.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row — the first row, against the BLOCK / CANONICAL / FINALITY / COST rows beneath it
findings.finding: The DATA row is roughly 260px tall; the four fact rows below it are roughly 40px each. One row is 62% of the card's height and the four values a reader came for occupy the bottom fifth. Row rhythm in the grid is therefore set by a nine-line paragraph in an unrelated cell, and the label column runs DATA … then 200px of empty grey before BLOCK, so the label spine is unscannable exactly where scanning is the point. The expectation asks whether the marker lands before a reader concludes anything about the empty sections; it does, but it lands by displacing the metadata the same expectation calls 'not a consolation prize'.

findings.location: page content column — Overview / Decoded input grids end at x≈1416, every notice card (Not observable, ABI note, Events, Internal calls, State changes) ends at x≈1203, in a 1920px viewport
findings.finding: The widest thing on the page is 911px and most of it is 697px, so 47% of a wide viewport carries all the content and the remainder is canvas on both sides. Nothing is dropped for the viewport and nothing is gained by it: the page is the mobile stack at desktop size. At this width the capture narrative and the four facts could sit side by side instead of the narrative pushing the facts 260px down, and the five single-paragraph notice cards each consume a full band of vertical space to carry two lines of text.

findings.location: Overview grid, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row — the value `0x00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000175c1a29c1f97278 mana (FeeJuice)`
findings.finding: A 64-digit hex word is printed in full to carry roughly 15 significant characters; the first 46 are zeros. There is no magnitude a reader can take from it at a glance and no comparison it supports against any other transaction, which is what a cost column is for. The label is the chain's camelCase field name uppercased and wrapped onto two lines with the separator dangling at the end of the first ("COST ·" / "TRANSACTIONFEE"), so the least legible value on the page also has the least legible label.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row prose vs the Not observable card above it
findings.finding: The pruning fact is told twice: the notice card explains that getTxByHash prunes at the finalized tip (block 67119) and this transaction settled at 67113, and the DATA paragraph roughly 350px below restates that transactions below 67119 have had their bodies pruned. Between the two restatements the DATA paragraph adds five sentences of capture statistics — 400 blocks enumerated, 20 transactions, a longest run of 309 empty blocks, advice about needing a follower that watches the tip — which are facts about the capture run, not about this transaction, and they are the densest text on a page whose reader is here for one hash.

findings.location: Decoded input section — the note card below the SELECTOR / RAW grid
findings.finding: "This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds, so the parameters are shown as raw bytes. Supplying an ABI decodes them." sits under `SELECTOR —` and `RAW 0x`, and the raw block at the foot of the page says `"bodyRetainedAtCapture": false`. There is no selector, no parameters and no raw bytes; the input is missing because the body was pruned. The copy therefore asserts a state that is not the one on screen, locates the limitation in this product's ABI holdings rather than in the chain's retention — the exact inversion the Not observable card gets right 900px above — and closes with a remedy a reader could act on that cannot succeed. Events, Internal calls and State changes each name their true, permanent reason; this section is the only one that does not, and it is the only place on the page where the voice makes a promise.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row — the paragraph under the `Real Aztec mainnet data` badge
findings.finding: The most important claim on the page is delivered in the capture tool's voice, not the product's. It shouts one sentence in caps ("NO TRANSACTION INSIDE IT WAS REPLAYABLE"), leaves machine plurals unresolved (`20 transaction(s)`, `6 block(s)`, `7 block(s)`), prints an internal build detail (`node 5.2.0`), and argues with an unseen sceptic ("That is what the capture found, not a failure to record"). Every other paragraph on the page — the Not observable card, the three section notes, the footer disclosure — is calm, third-person and specific. A marketing-grade surface cannot publish a log line at the one point where it states what its data is; the register break is most visible precisely where credibility matters most.

findings.location: Overview grid, DATA row, sentences 4–8, against the Not observable card above it
findings.finding: The page explains itself twice in two different voices. The Not observable card explains pruning as a fact about this transaction; the DATA row re-explains pruning plus the capture run's statistics — 400 blocks enumerated, a longest run of 309 empty blocks, advice that catching a replayable transaction "needs a follower that watches the tip continuously rather than a single scan". That last is an operational note to whoever runs the capture, addressed to a reader who came for one hash. The doubling weakens the single reason the expectation wants taken away, because the second telling is longer, louder and mostly about something else.

findings.location: Overview grid, label column — `COST · TRANSACTIONFEE` against `BLOCK`, `CANONICAL`, `FINALITY`, `DATA`
findings.finding: Four labels are the product's own vocabulary, one is the chain's camelCase field name uppercased and bolted to it with a middle dot, wrapping onto two lines. Whatever the dot is meant to disclose — the product's word and the node's field — it reads as an unfinished mapping between two vocabularies, and it appears only on the row whose value is also raw chain output. The rest of the grid establishes that this product names things in its own words; this row is where that stops.
